translations.literal: Volume Eighteen, Treatise Eight.

sentences.zh: 律曆志下

translations.literal: Treatise on Pitch-Pipes and the Calendar, Part Three.
translations.idiomatic: Treatise on Harmonics and Calendrics, part three (section title).

sentences.zh: 魏尚書郎楊偉表曰：「臣覽載籍，斷考歷數，時以紀農，月以紀事，其所由來，遐而尚矣。

translations.literal: Yang Wei, Gentleman of the Secretariat of Wei, presented a memorial saying: “Your servant has perused the records, reckoned and examined calendrical numbers: the seasons are used to mark the farming year, the months to mark affairs; how this practice arose lies far in antiquity and has long been honored.”
translations.idiomatic: Yang Wei, a Wei Secretariat official, wrote: “I have combed the sources and worked through the calendar’s numbers: seasons organize agriculture, months organize administration—and that arrangement goes back to remote antiquity.”

sentences.zh: 乃自少昊，則玄鳥司分，顓頊、帝嚳，則重黎司天；

translations.literal: From Shao Hao onward, the Dark Bird (Xuan Niao) presided over the equinoxes; Zhuan Xu and Di Ku had Chong and Li regulate Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Already under Shao Hao the swallow asterism marked the equinoxes; under Zhuan Xu and Di Ku, Chong and Li were charged with celestial regulation.

sentences.zh: 唐帝、虞舜，則羲和掌日，三代因之，則世有日官。

translations.literal: Under the Tang Emperor and Shun of Yu, Xi and He managed the sun; the Three Dynasties continued this, so each age had sun officers.
translations.idiomatic: The legendary rulers Yao and Shun placed Xi and He in charge of the solar calendar; the three early dynasties kept the office, so every reign maintained “sun” specialists.

sentences.zh: 日官司曆，則頒之諸侯，諸侯受之，則頒於境內。

translations.literal: The sun officers managed the calendar, then promulgated it to the feudal lords; the lords received it and promulgated it within their domains.
translations.idiomatic: Those officers set the calendar and issued it to the regional lords, who in turn published it inside their own territories.

sentences.zh: 夏後之世，羲和湎淫，廢時亂日，則《書》載《胤征》。

translations.literal: In the age after the Xia, Xi and He sank into debauchery, neglected the seasons and threw the days into confusion, so the Documents records the “Punitive Expedition of Yin.”
translations.idiomatic: Later in the Xia era, Xi and He neglected their duty, deranged the calendar, which is why the *Book of Documents* preserves the “Yin” punitive campaign against them.

sentences.zh: 由此觀之，審農時而重人事，歷代然之也。

translations.literal: Viewed from this, scrutinizing the farming seasons and taking human affairs seriously has been the constant practice of successive dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: From this it is clear that every dynasty has treated careful timing for agriculture and attention to civic order as a standing principle.

sentences.zh: 逮至周室既衰，戰國橫鶩，告朔之羊，廢而不紹，登臺之禮，滅而不遵，閏分乖次而不識，孟陬失紀而莫悟，大火猶西流，而怪蟄蟲之不藏也。

translations.literal: When it came to the decline of the Zhou house, the Warring States ran rampant: the sheep for the “first-day-of-month” announcement was abandoned and not renewed; the observatory rites perished and were not observed; intercalary divisions fell out of sequence and went unrecognized; the first month lost its reckoning and no one corrected it; the Great Fire still streamed westward, yet people wondered that hibernating insects did not hide away.
translations.idiomatic: By late Zhou the realm fractured: monthly temple announcements lapsed, observatory ceremonies died out, leap months drifted out of place, and the civil year’s first month wandered—while Antares still hung in the western sky, courtiers marveled at insects that failed to burrow, blind to the calendar’s chaos.

sentences.zh: 是時也，天子不協時，司曆不書日。

translations.literal: At that time the Son of Heaven did not harmonize the seasons, and the calendar officers did not record the days.
translations.idiomatic: The king no longer coordinated the seasons, and official scribes stopped reliably dating events.

sentences.zh: 諸侯不受職，日禦不分朔，人事不恤，廢棄農時。

translations.literal: The feudal lords did not accept their duties; the day-keepers did not fix new-moon days; human affairs went untended and the farming seasons were cast aside.
translations.idiomatic: Regional rulers ignored their responsibilities, astronomers lost track of true conjunctions, and governance neglected both people and the agricultural timetable.

sentences.zh: 仲尼之撥亂於《春秋》，托褒貶糾正，司曆失閏，則譏而書之，登臺頒朔，則謂之有禮。

translations.literal: Confucius, in setting right disorder through the *Spring and Autumn Annals*, relied on praise and blame to correct matters: when calendar officers missed intercalations he ridiculed and recorded it; when they ascended the observatory to issue the new-moon calendar he called that observance of ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius used the *Spring and Autumn* to restore order through moral judgment: he mocked missed intercalations, yet praised rulers who climbed the terrace to proclaim the civil calendar as behaving ritually.

sentences.zh: 自此以降，暨于秦漢，乃復以孟冬為歲首，閏為後九月，中節乖錯，時月紕繆。

translations.literal: From this downward to Qin and Han, they again took the tenth winter month as year-beginning, placed intercalary months after the ninth month, so mid-term solar nodes and civil months went awry.
translations.idiomatic: Down through Qin and Han the year again began in early winter, leap months were tacked after the ninth month, and solar terms and lunar months slipped badly out of alignment.

sentences.zh: 加時後天，蝕不在朔，累載相襲，久而不革也。

translations.literal: The added hours lagged behind Heaven; eclipses no longer fell on new-moon days; age after age inherited the error and long delayed reform.
translations.idiomatic: Ephemeris corrections ran behind the sky, eclipses missed conjunction, and the mistake persisted reign after reign without overhaul.

sentences.zh: 至武帝元封七年，始乃悟其繆焉，於是改正朔，更歷數，使大才通人，更造《太初曆》，校中朔所差，以正閏分，課中星得度，以考疏密，以建寅之月為正朔，以黃鐘之月為曆初。

translations.literal: It was not until the seventh year of Yuanfeng of Emperor Wu that the error was grasped; thereupon the beginning of the year was corrected, calendrical numbers were changed, great talents and learned men were ordered to compose the *Grand Inception Calendar*, the discrepancy at mid-conjunction was checked to fix the intercalary fraction, mid-heaven stars were verified for angular position to test tightness or looseness, the month with *jianyin* was taken as standard new year, and the month of the yellow-bell pitch-pipe as calendrical origin.
translations.idiomatic: Only in 104 BCE did Emperor Wu recognize the fault: he reformed the civil calendar, commissioned the *Taichu* system, adjusted the leap fraction against true conjunctions, checked stellar longitudes, adopted *jianyin* (roughly late winter) as the first month of the year, and anchored the epoch in the “yellow bell” month.

sentences.zh: 其曆斗分太多，後遂疏闊。

translations.literal: That calendar’s dipper fraction was too large, and in later times it became coarse and loose.
translations.idiomatic: The Taichu system’s fractional remainder for the Dipper was too big, so in later reigns it grew increasingly imprecise.

sentences.zh: 至元和二年，復用《四分曆》，施而行之，至於今日，考察日蝕，率常在晦，是則斗分太多，故先密後疏而不可用也。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanhe they reverted to the *Quarter-Day Calendar*, applied it down to the present; examining solar eclipses, they almost always occur on the last day of the month—thus the dipper fraction was too large, so it was first tight and later loose and unusable.
translations.idiomatic: From 85 CE the *Sifen* (quarter-day) calendar returned; eclipse records show conjunctions drifting to month-end—proof the fractional excess was too large, yielding an apparently tight fit that soon loosened into uselessness.

sentences.zh: 是以臣前以制典餘日，推考天路，稽之前典，驗之以蝕朔，詳而精之，更建密曆，則不先不後，古今中天。

translations.literal: Therefore your servant, using the surplus days of the statutory canon, traced the celestial track, collated earlier classics, tested with eclipse and conjunction data, refined it in detail, and established a tighter calendar so that neither early nor late it stands midway between ancient and modern mid-heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Hence I reworked the official surplus-day reckoning, checked it against eclipses and prior canons, and drew up a denser calendar that tracks the sky evenly—neither ahead nor behind—between antiquity and today.

sentences.zh: 以昔在唐帝，協日正時，允厘百工，咸熙庶績也。

translations.literal: Thus in antiquity under Emperor Yao the days were harmonized and the seasons rectified, so the hundred crafts were duly assigned and the myriad tasks flourished.
translations.idiomatic: This matches Yao’s age, when aligning the days and seasons allowed every office to function and every undertaking to thrive.

sentences.zh: 欲使當今國之典禮，凡百制度，皆韜合往古，鬱然備足，乃改正朔，更歷數，以大呂之月為歲首，以建子之月為曆初。

translations.literal: He desires that the state’s canonical rites and the hundred institutions should all fold together with antiquity and stand complete; therefore he corrects the beginning of the year, changes calendrical numbers, takes the month of the great *lü* as year-head, and the month with *jianzi* as calendrical origin.
translations.idiomatic: He wants current state ritual and every institution to echo ancient models; so he resets the civil year, revises the calendrical constants, begins the year in the great-*lü* month, and sets the computational epoch in the *jianzi* month.

sentences.zh: 臣以為昔在帝代，則法曰《顓頊》，曩自軒轅，則曆曰《黃帝》，暨至漢之孝武，革正朔，更歷數，改元曰太初，因名《太初曆》。

translations.literal: Your servant holds that in the age of the emperors the method was called *Zhuanxu*; from the Yellow Emperor onward the calendar was called *Yellow Emperor*; down to Emperor Xiaowu of Han, who corrected the beginning of the year, changed calendrical numbers, and altered the reign title to Taichu, whence it was named the *Taichu Calendar*.
translations.idiomatic: I note that each great reform named its system—*Zhuanxu*, the Yellow Emperor’s calendar, and Han Wudi’s *Taichu* calendar after his new era name.

sentences.zh: 今改元為景初，宜曰《景初曆》。

translations.literal: Now that the era name is changed to Jingchu, it should be titled the *Jingchu Calendar*.
translations.idiomatic: Since the reign era is now Jingchu, the new system ought to be called the *Jingchu* calendar.

sentences.zh: 臣之所建《景初曆》，法數則約要，施用則近密，治之則省功，學之則易知。

translations.literal: As for the *Jingchu Calendar* your servant has devised, its constants are concise, in use it is close and dense, to administer it saves labor, and to study it is easy to understand.
translations.idiomatic: The *Jingchu* scheme I propose keeps the parameters lean yet numerically tight, runs efficiently in practice, and is straightforward to learn.

sentences.zh: 雖復使研桑心算，隸首運籌，重黎司晷，羲和察景，以考天路，步驗日月，究極精微，盡術數之極者，皆未能並臣如此之妙也。

translations.literal: Even if one employed Yanzi’s merchant reckoning, Lishou’s counting rods, Chong and Li on the gnomon, Xi and He observing shadows, to investigate the celestial road, pace and verify sun and moon, exhaust the utmost fineness and reach the limit of computation, none could match the subtlety your servant has attained.
translations.idiomatic: No amount of legendary arithmetical skill—merchant Yan’s mental sums, Lishou’s rods, Chong and Li at the sundial, Xi and He at the solstice shadow—could match the precision I have reached.

sentences.zh: 是以累代歷數，皆疏而不密，自黃帝以來，常改革不已。」

translations.literal: Therefore the calendrical numbers of successive ages have all been loose rather than tight; from the Yellow Emperor onward they have been repeatedly reformed without end.”
translations.idiomatic: That is why earlier dynasties’ calendars always erred on the loose side, and why reform has followed reform ever since the Yellow Emperor.”

sentences.zh: 壬辰以來，至景初元年丁已歲，積四千四十六，算上。

translations.literal: From the *gengchen* epoch down to the first year of Jingchu, the *dingsi* year, the accumulated count is 4046, counted on the stem.
translations.idiomatic: From the Gengchen origin through the Jingchu era’s first year (a Dingsi year in the cycle), the accumulated count is 4046, inclusive on the upper stem count.

sentences.zh: 此元以天正建子黃鐘之月為曆初，元首之歲，夜半甲子朔旦冬至。

translations.literal: This origin takes the celestial-standard month with *jianzi* and the yellow-bell month as calendrical beginning; in the year of the origin’s head, at midnight on *jiazi* new moon and winter solstice coincide.
translations.idiomatic: The epoch uses the true winter month (*jianzi*) aligned with the yellow-bell pitch month as calendar zero, so at the origin year’s start a Jiazi day begins at midnight exactly at winter solstice.

sentences.zh: 求其數之所生者，置一紀積月，以通數乘之，會通去之，所去之余，紀差之數也。

sentences.zh: 以之轉加前紀，則得後紀。

translations.literal: By rotating and subtracting it from the preceding cycle, one obtains the following cycle.
translations.idiomatic: Subtract that decrement from the prior cycle’s anomaly rate to obtain the next.

sentences.zh: 不足減者，加通周。

translations.literal: If subtraction is insufficient, add the passage cycle.
translations.idiomatic: If you cannot subtract, add the passage cycle first.

sentences.zh: 求次元紀差率，轉減前元甲寅紀差率，餘則次元甲子紀差率也。

translations.literal: To seek the next-origin cycle difference rate, rotate-subtract the prior-origin Jiayin-cycle difference rate; the remainder is the next-origin Jiazi-cycle difference rate.
translations.idiomatic: For the next grand origin, subtract the previous Jiayin-cycle rate from the Jiazi-cycle rate as prescribed to get the new Jiazi increment.

sentences.zh: 求次紀，如上法也。

translations.literal: To seek the next cycle, use the method above.
translations.idiomatic: To advance to the following cycle, repeat the same rule.

sentences.zh: 推朔積月術曰：置壬辰元以來，盡所求年，外所求，以紀法除之，所得算外，所入紀第也，余則入紀年數也。

translations.literal: Method for pushing accumulated months from new moons: set the *renchen* origin through the year sought, excluding the sought year itself, divide by the cycle divisor; the obtained count outside the division is which cycle you have entered, and the remainder is the years entered within the cycle.
translations.idiomatic: To count lunations from the Gengchen epoch up to (but not including) the target year, divide by 1,843: the quotient (plus one) gives the cycle index, the remainder the year within that cycle.

sentences.zh: 以章月乘之，如章歲而一，為積月，不盡為閏餘。

translations.literal: Multiply by cycle months and divide by cycle years to obtain accumulated months; what does not exhaust is the intercalary remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply that year-count by 22,795 and divide by 19 for total months; the remainder is the leap fraction.

sentences.zh: 閏餘十二以上，其年有閏。

translations.literal: If the intercalary remainder is twelve or more, that year has an intercalary month.
translations.idiomatic: A leap year occurs when the intercalary remainder reaches twelve or higher.

sentences.zh: 閏月以無中氣為正。

translations.literal: An intercalary month is determined by having no mid-climate in the month.
translations.idiomatic: The leap month is the lunar month that contains no major solar term.

sentences.zh: 推朔術曰：以通數乘積月，為朔積分。

translations.literal: Method for pushing new moons: multiply accumulated months by the common multiple to obtain the accumulated new-moon fraction.
translations.idiomatic: To compute conjunction instants, multiply accumulated months by 134,630.

sentences.zh: 如日法而一，為積日，不盡為小餘。

translations.literal: Divide by the day divisor to obtain accumulated days; what does not exhaust is the small remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Divide that product by 4,559 for whole days; the residue is the fractional day.

sentences.zh: 以六十去積日，余為大餘。

translations.literal: Remove sixties from accumulated days; the remainder is the large remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Reduce the day count modulo sixty for the sexagenary stem-branch index.

sentences.zh: 大餘命以紀，算外，所求年天正十一月朔日也。

translations.literal: Count the large remainder by the cycle, outside the reckoning: this is the new-moon day of the eleventh civil month of the year sought.
translations.idiomatic: Index that remainder against the sexagenary cycle to name the day of the eleventh month’s conjunction in the target civil year.

sentences.zh: 求次月，加大餘二十九，小餘二千四百一十九，小餘滿日法從大餘，命如前，次月朔日也。

translations.literal: To seek the next month, add to the large remainder 29, to the small remainder 2419; when the small remainder fills the day divisor, carry to the large remainder; count as before: this is the next month’s conjunction day.
translations.idiomatic: For the following month add 29 to the day count and 2,419 to the fraction, carrying overflows by 4,559 into the day count, then read off the next conjunction.

sentences.zh: 小餘二千一百四十以上，其月大也。

translations.literal: If the small remainder is 2140 or more, that month is long.
translations.idiomatic: If the fractional part is 2,140 or greater, the month is a long (30-day) month.

sentences.zh: 推弦望，加朔大餘七，小餘千七百四十四，小分一，小分滿二從小餘，小餘滿日法從大餘，大餘滿六十去之，余命以紀，算外，上弦日也。

translations.literal: To push first and third quarters and full moons: add to the new-moon large remainder seven, to the small remainder 1744, and to the minute fraction one; when the minute fraction fills two, carry to the small remainder; when the small remainder fills the day divisor, carry to the large remainder; when the large remainder fills sixty, remove it; the remainder counted by the cycle, outside the reckoning, is the first-quarter day.
translations.idiomatic: For quarters: add 7 days, 1,744 parts, and one small part to the new-moon line, propagating carries through the small-part, fractional-day, and sexagenary levels; the result names the first-quarter day.

sentences.zh: 又加，得望、下弦、後月朔。

translations.literal: Again adding, one obtains full moon, last quarter, and the next month’s new moon.
translations.idiomatic: Repeat the same addition chain to reach full moon, third quarter, and the next conjunction.

sentences.zh: 其月蝕望者，定小餘如在中節者定小餘如所近中節間限數、限數以下者，算上為日。

translations.literal: For a month in which the moon is eclipsed at opposition, settle the small remainder; if it falls at the mid-term node, settle the small remainder by the gap-limit number of the nearest mid-term; if it is at or below the limit number, count upward and treat it as a day.
translations.idiomatic: When a lunar eclipse falls on the full moon, adjust the fractional day so that, if the value sits on the major solar term, you align it with that term’s margin limits; anything at or under the limit rounds up to count as a full day.

sentences.zh: 望在中節前後各四日以還者，視限數；

translations.literal: If opposition falls within four days on either side of the mid-term node, consult the limit number.
translations.idiomatic: When full moon lies within four days before or after the major term, use the standard limit figure.

sentences.zh: 望在中節前後各五日以上者，視間限。

translations.literal: If opposition falls five or more days before or after the mid-term node, consult the gap limit.
translations.idiomatic: When full moon sits five or more days away from the major term, switch to the wider gap-limit criterion instead.

sentences.zh: 推二十四氣術曰：置所入紀年，外所求，以餘數乘之，滿紀法為大餘，不盡為小餘。

translations.literal: Method for computing the twenty-four qi: set the years entered in the cycle, excluding the year sought, multiply by the remainder number; what fills the cycle divisor becomes the large remainder, what does not exhaust is the small remainder.
translations.idiomatic: To place the twenty-four solar terms: take years elapsed within the current cycle (not counting the target year), multiply by 9,670, divide by 1,843 for the day count, and keep the fractional remainder.

sentences.zh: 大餘滿六十去之，余命以紀，算外，天正十一月冬至日也。

translations.literal: Remove sixties from the large remainder; count the remainder by the cycle, outside the reckoning: this is the winter-solstice day of the eleventh civil month of the celestial-standard year.
translations.idiomatic: Reduce the day line modulo sixty and read it against the sexagenary cycle to name the winter solstice of the eleventh month.

sentences.zh: 求次氣，加大餘十五，小餘四百二，小分十一，小分滿氣法從小餘，小餘滿紀法從大餘，命如前，次氣日也。

translations.literal: To seek the next qi, add to the large remainder fifteen, to the small remainder 402, to the minute fraction eleven; when the minute fraction fills the qi divisor, carry to the small remainder; when the small remainder fills the cycle divisor, carry to the large remainder; count as before: this is the next qi day.
translations.idiomatic: For each successive term add 15 days, 402 parts, and 11 minute-fractions, carrying overflows through the fractional hierarchy as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 推閏月術曰：以閏余減章歲，餘以歲中乘之，滿章閏得一月，余滿半法以上，亦得一月。

translations.literal: Method for seeking the intercalary month: subtract the intercalary remainder from the cycle years; multiply the remainder by months per year; divide by intercalations per cycle to obtain one month; if the remainder fills half the divisor or more, again obtain one month.
translations.idiomatic: To find leap months: subtract the leap fraction from 19, multiply the residue by 12, divide by 7, and add an extra leap month whenever the remainder reaches half the divisor.

sentences.zh: 數從天正十一月起，算外，閏月也。

translations.literal: Count starting from the eleventh civil month of the celestial-standard year, outside the reckoning: that is the intercalary month.
translations.idiomatic: Count forward from the eleventh month; the slot so reached is the intercalary month.

sentences.zh: 閏有進退，以無中氣禦之。

translations.literal: Intercalations may advance or retreat; one controls them by the rule that no mid-climate may fall inside the month.
translations.idiomatic: Leap placement can shift forward or back, but the governing rule remains “no major solar term within the leap month.”

translations.literal: Spring Equinox, second month, median term: limit number 1008, gap limit 979.
translations.idiomatic: Spring equinox (2nd month, major term): margin 1008, gap margin 979.

translations.literal: Clear and Bright, third month, node: limit number 951, gap limit 925.
translations.idiomatic: Clear and bright (3rd month, node): margin 951, gap margin 925.

translations.literal: Grain Rain, third month, median term: limit number 900, gap limit 879.
translations.idiomatic: Grain rain (3rd month, major term): margin 900, gap margin 879.

translations.idiomatic: Grain fills (4th month, major term): margin 823, gap margin 812.

translations.idiomatic: Grain in ear (5th month, node): margin 800, gap margin 799.

translations.literal: Summer Solstice, fifth month, median term: limit number 798, gap limit 801.
translations.idiomatic: Summer solstice (5th month, major term): margin 798, gap margin 801.

translations.idiomatic: Minor heat (6th month, node): margin 805, gap margin 815.

translations.idiomatic: Major heat (6th month, major term): margin 825, gap margin 842.

translations.idiomatic: End of heat (7th month, major term): margin 907, gap margin 935.

translations.idiomatic: White dew (8th month, node): margin 962, gap margin 992.

translations.idiomatic: Minor snow (10th month, major term): margin 1215, gap margin 1229.

sentences.zh: 推沒滅術曰：因冬至積日有小餘者，加積一，以沒分乘之，以沒法除之，所得為大餘，不盡為小餘。

translations.literal: Method for pushing “oblivion” and extinction: if the accumulated days from winter solstice have a small remainder, add one to the accumulated count; multiply by the oblivion numerator and divide by the oblivion divisor; the quotient is the large remainder, the non-exhausting part the small remainder.
translations.idiomatic: To locate hidden days after the solstice line: if a fractional day remains, increment the day count, multiply by 67,315, divide by 967, and split quotient and remainder.

sentences.zh: 大餘滿六十去之，余命以紀，算外，即去年冬至後日也。

translations.literal: Remove sixties from the large remainder; count the remainder by the cycle, outside the reckoning: this is the day after last year’s winter solstice.
translations.idiomatic: The sexagenary index so obtained dates the day immediately following the previous winter solstice.

sentences.zh: 求次沒，加大餘六十九，小餘五百九十二，小餘滿沒法得一，從大餘，命如前。

translations.literal: To seek the next oblivion, add to the large remainder sixty-nine, to the small remainder 592; when the small remainder fills the oblivion divisor, obtain one and carry to the large remainder; count as before.
translations.idiomatic: For each successive hidden day add 69 days and 592 parts, carrying a full 967 parts into the day count.

sentences.zh: 小餘盡，為滅也。

translations.literal: When the small remainder is exhausted, that is extinction.
translations.idiomatic: A zero fractional part marks the extinction point of the sequence.

sentences.zh: 推五行用事日：立春、立夏、立秋、立冬者，即木、火、金、水始用事日也。

translations.literal: Method for pushing the days when the Five Phases take charge: Spring Begins, Summer Begins, Autumn Begins, and Winter Begins are the days when wood, fire, metal, and water respectively begin their governance.
translations.idiomatic: The four “begins” mark the days when wood, fire, metal, and water each assume seasonal authority.

sentences.zh: 各減其大餘十八，小餘四百八十三，小分六，余命以紀，算外，各四立之前，土用事日也。

translations.literal: For each, subtract from its large remainder eighteen, from its small remainder 483, from its minute fraction six; count the remainder by the cycle, outside the reckoning: these are the days before each of the four “established” seasons when earth takes charge.
translations.idiomatic: Subtract 18 days, 483 parts, and 6 minute-fractions from each term line to reach the earth-phase days before the solstices and equinoxes.

sentences.zh: 大餘不足減者，加六十；

translations.literal: If the large remainder is insufficient for subtraction, add sixty.
translations.idiomatic: If the day line underflows, borrow sixty days.

sentences.zh: 小餘不足者，減大餘一，加紀法；

translations.literal: If the small remainder is insufficient, subtract one from the large remainder and add the cycle divisor.
translations.idiomatic: If the fractional parts underflow, decrement the day count and add 1,843 to the fraction.

sentences.zh: 小分不足減者，減小餘一，加氣法。

translations.literal: If the minute fraction is insufficient for subtraction, subtract one from the small remainder and add the qi divisor.
translations.idiomatic: If minute-fractions underflow, borrow one small-remainder unit and add twelve minute-fractions.

sentences.zh: 推卦用事日：因冬至大餘，六其小餘，即《坎卦》用事日也。

translations.literal: Method for pushing the days when the hexagrams take charge: from the winter-solstice large remainder, multiply its small remainder by six: that is the day when the *Kan* hexagram takes charge.
translations.idiomatic: Starting at the winter solstice line, multiply the fractional day by six to place the *Kan* hexagram’s governing day.

sentences.zh: 加小餘萬九十一，滿元法從大餘，即《中孚》用事日也。

translations.literal: Add small remainder 10,091; when it fills the origin divisor, carry to the large remainder: that is the day when *Zhong Fu* takes charge.
translations.idiomatic: Then add 10,091 fractional parts (carrying at 11,058) to reach the *Zhong fu* governing day.

sentences.zh: 求次卦，各加大餘六，小餘九百六十七。

translations.literal: To seek the next hexagram, to each add large remainder six, small remainder 967.
translations.idiomatic: Each following hexagram advances the line by six days and 967 parts.

sentences.zh: 其四正各因其中日，六其小餘。

translations.literal: For the four “correct” hexagrams, in each case take its mid-day line and multiply the small remainder by six.
translations.idiomatic: For the four cardinal hexagrams, multiply that term’s fractional day by six instead.

sentences.zh: 推日度術曰：以紀法朔積日，滿周天去之，余以紀法除之，所得為度，不盡為分。

translations.literal: Method for pushing solar longitude: take accumulated new-moon days with the cycle divisor, remove multiples of the full circle; divide the remainder by the cycle divisor; the quotient is degrees, what does not exhaust is minutes.
translations.idiomatic: To find the sun’s degree: reduce the lunation day count modulo 673,150, then divide by 1,843 for degrees and minutes of arc.

sentences.zh: 命度從牛前五起，宿次除之，不滿宿，則天正十一月朔夜半日所在度及分也。

translations.literal: Count degrees starting five ahead of Ox; remove by lodge sequence; what does not fill a lodge is the degree and minute where the sun stands at the eleventh month’s new-moon midnight of the celestial-standard year.
translations.idiomatic: Begin counting five degrees before the Ox lodge and step through the twenty-eight mansions to locate the sun at midnight on the eleventh month’s conjunction.

sentences.zh: 求次日，日加一度，分不加，經鬥除斗分，分少，退一度。

translations.literal: To seek the next day, add one degree to the sun without adding minutes; when passing through the Dipper, remove the dipper fraction; if minutes are short, retreat one degree.
translations.idiomatic: Advance one degree per civil day, drop the dipper correction when crossing that mansion, and borrow a degree if minutes run short.

sentences.zh: 推月度術曰：以月周乘朔積日，滿周天去之，余以紀法除之，所得為度，不盡為分，命如上法，則天正十一月朔夜半月所在度及分也。

translations.literal: Method for pushing lunar longitude: multiply accumulated new-moon days by the lunar circuit, remove multiples of the full circle; divide the remainder by the cycle divisor; the quotient is degrees, what does not exhaust is minutes; count as in the method above: this is the degree and minute where the moon stands at the eleventh month’s new-moon midnight of the celestial-standard year.
translations.idiomatic: For the moon, multiply the same day count by 24,638, reduce modulo the full circle, divide by 1,843, and read mansions as for the sun.

sentences.zh: 求次月，小月加度二十二，分八百六，大月又加一日，度十三，分六百七十九；

translations.literal: To seek the next month, for a short month add twenty-two degrees, 806 minutes; for a long month further add one day, thirteen degrees, 679 minutes.
translations.idiomatic: Short months advance the moon 22°806′; long months add another day plus 13°679′.

sentences.zh: 分滿紀法得一度，則並月朔夜半月所在度分及也。

translations.literal: When minutes fill the cycle divisor, obtain one degree; then together you have the degree and minute of the moon at that month’s new-moon midnight.
translations.idiomatic: Carry 1,843 arc-minutes into one degree to finish the moon’s position at conjunction midnight.

sentences.zh: 其冬下旬，月在張、心署之。

translations.literal: In the last third of winter, note the moon among *Zhang* and *Heart*.
translations.idiomatic: During late winter the text records the moon among the *Zhang* and *Heart* lodges.

sentences.zh: 推合朔度術曰：以章歲乘朔小餘，滿通法為大分，不盡為小分。

translations.literal: Method for pushing conjunction longitude: multiply the new moon’s small remainder by cycle years; what fills the passage divisor is the large minute, what does not exhaust is the small minute.
translations.idiomatic: To combine sun–moon longitude at conjunction: multiply the conjunction fraction by 19 and divide by 47 for large and small arc-parts.

sentences.zh: 以大分從朔夜半日度分，分滿紀法從度，命如前，則天正十一月合朔日月所共合度也。

translations.literal: Add the large minute to the sun’s degree and minute at new-moon midnight; when minutes fill the cycle divisor, carry to degrees; count as before: this is the shared conjunction longitude of sun and moon in the eleventh month of the celestial-standard year.
translations.idiomatic: Add those parts to the solar position at conjunction midnight, carrying arc-units into degrees to get the common ecliptic longitude.

sentences.zh: 求次月，加度二十九，大分九百七十七，小分四十二，小分滿通法從大分，大分滿紀法從度，經鬥除其分，則次月合朔日月所共合度也。

translations.literal: To seek the next month, add twenty-nine degrees, large minute 977, small minute 42; when small minutes fill the passage divisor, carry to the large minute; when the large minute fills the cycle divisor, carry to degrees; when passing through the Dipper remove its fraction: this is the next month’s shared conjunction longitude of sun and moon.
translations.idiomatic: Each lunation adds 29°977′42″ of arc, with carries through the passage and cycle divisors and a dipper correction.

sentences.zh: 推弦望日所在度：加合朔度七，大分七百五，小分十，微分一，微分滿二從小分，小分滿通法從大分，大分滿紀法從度，命如前，則上弦日所在度也。

translations.literal: To push the sun’s degree at first quarter and full moon: add to the conjunction longitude seven degrees, large minute 705, small minute ten, micro-fraction one; when micro-fraction fills two, carry to small minute; when small minute fills the passage divisor, carry to large minute; when large minute fills the cycle divisor, carry to degrees; count as before: this is the sun’s degree at first quarter.
translations.idiomatic: Quarters add fixed degree increments with micro-fraction carries to place the sun at first quarter.

sentences.zh: 又加，得望，下弦、後月合也。

translations.literal: Again adding, one obtains full moon, last quarter, and the next month’s conjunction.
translations.idiomatic: Repeat the addition to reach full moon, third quarter, and the following new moon.

sentences.zh: 推弦望月所在度：加合朔度九十八，大分千二百七十九，小分三十四，數滿命如前，即上弦月所在度也。

translations.literal: To push the moon’s degree at first quarter and full moon: add to the conjunction longitude ninety-eight degrees, large minute 1279, small minute thirty-four; when counts fill, count as before: this is the moon’s degree at first quarter.
translations.idiomatic: The moon’s first-quarter position adds 98°1279′34″ to the conjunction longitude with the same carry rules.

sentences.zh: 又加，得望，下弦、後月合也。

translations.literal: Again adding, one obtains full moon, last quarter, and the next month’s conjunction.
translations.idiomatic: Iterate to obtain full moon, last quarter, and the next conjunction line for the moon.

sentences.zh: 推日月昏明度術曰：日以紀法，月以月周，乘所近節氣夜漏，二百而一，為明分。

translations.literal: Method for pushing the dusk and dawn positions of sun and moon: multiply the night clepsydra of the nearest solar term by the cycle divisor for the sun and by the lunar circuit for the moon; divide by two hundred to obtain the bright fraction.
translations.idiomatic: Scale the night water-clock reading of the neighboring qi by 1,843 for the sun or 24,638 for the moon, then divide by 200 for the daylight segment.

sentences.zh: 日以減紀法，月以減月周，餘為昏分。

translations.literal: For the sun subtract from the cycle divisor, for the moon subtract from the lunar circuit; the remainders are the dusk fractions.
translations.idiomatic: Subtract those products from the respective divisors to isolate the twilight segments.

sentences.zh: 各以分加夜半，如法為度。

translations.literal: To each fraction add the midnight value; according to the rule they become degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Add each segment to the midnight longitude and reduce by the usual degree rule.

sentences.zh: 推合朔交會月蝕術曰：置所入紀朔積分，以所入紀下交會差率之數加之，以會通去之，餘則所求年天正十一月合朔去交度分也。

translations.literal: Method for pushing conjunction, node crossing, and lunar eclipse: set the accumulated new-moon fraction for the cycle entered, add to it the conjunction–node difference rate listed under that cycle, remove multiples of the conjunction product; the remainder is the degrees and minutes from the node at the eleventh month’s new moon of the year sought.
translations.idiomatic: Combine the lunation fraction with the tabulated node-difference rate and reduce modulo 790,110 to find nodal distance at civil-year conjunction.

sentences.zh: 以通數加之，滿會通去之，餘則次月合朔去交度分也。

translations.literal: Add the common multiple; remove multiples of the conjunction product; the remainder is the next month’s degrees and minutes from the node at new moon.
translations.idiomatic: Add 134,630 repeatedly modulo 790,110 for successive new moons.

sentences.zh: 以朔望合數各加其月合朔去交度分，滿會通去之，餘則各其月望去交度分也。

translations.literal: Add to each month’s new-moon nodal distance the lunation conjunction–opposition constants; remove multiples of the conjunction product; the remainders are that month’s degrees and minutes from the node at full moon.
translations.idiomatic: Add the conjunction–opposition offsets to get full-moon nodal distances similarly.

sentences.zh: 朔望去交分，如朔望合數以下，入交限數以上者，朔則交會，望則月蝕。

translations.literal: If the new- or full-moon nodal fraction is below the conjunction–opposition sum yet above the node-crossing limit, then at new moon there is a solar eclipse, at full moon a lunar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: When the nodal residue lies between the tabulated inner and outer thresholds, expect a solar eclipse at conjunction or a lunar eclipse at opposition.

sentences.zh: 推合朔交會月蝕月在日道表裏術曰：置所入紀朔積分，以所入紀下交會差率之數加之，倍會通去之，餘不滿會通者，紀首表，天正合朔月在表；

translations.literal: Method for pushing whether the moon at conjunction, node crossing, and eclipse lies inside or outside the solar path: set the accumulated new-moon fraction for the cycle entered, add the listed conjunction–node difference rate, remove double multiples of the conjunction product; if the remainder does not fill the conjunction product, the cycle head is outside, and the eleventh month’s new moon moon is outside.
translations.idiomatic: Halve the modulo arithmetic on the nodal sum: a remainder under half the product marks the moon outside the ecliptic at the year’s first conjunction.

sentences.zh: 紀首裏，天正合朔月在裏。

translations.literal: If the cycle head is inside, the eleventh month’s new-moon moon is inside.
translations.idiomatic: If the half-modulo test marks the cycle head as inside, the new moon lies inside the solar track.

sentences.zh: 滿會通去之，表滿在裏，裏滿在表。

translations.literal: Remove multiples of the conjunction product; when outside is full, it is inside; when inside is full, it is outside.
translations.idiomatic: Each full wrap of the conjunction product toggles the moon from outside to inside the ecliptic or the reverse.

sentences.zh: 求次月，以通數加之，滿會通去之，加里滿在表，加表滿在裏。

translations.literal: To seek the next month, add the common multiple, remove multiples of the conjunction product; add inside, when full go to outside; add outside, when full go to inside.
translations.idiomatic: For later months add 134,630 modulo 790,110 and flip inside/outside whenever the running sum crosses the product boundary.

sentences.zh: 先交會後月蝕者，朔在表則望在表，朔在裹則望在裏。

translations.literal: When node crossing precedes eclipse, if new moon is outside then full moon is outside; if new moon is inside then full moon is inside.
translations.idiomatic: If the node is crossed before opposition, inside and outside states match at new and full moons.

sentences.zh: 先月蝕後交會者，看蝕月朔在裏則望在表，朔在表則望在裏。

translations.literal: When eclipse precedes node crossing, observe the eclipse month: if new moon is inside then full moon is outside; if new moon is outside then full moon is inside.
translations.idiomatic: If the eclipse occurs before the node, new moon and full moon sit on opposite sides of the ecliptic.

sentences.zh: 交會月蝕如朔望合數以下，則前交後會；

translations.literal: If conjunction eclipse and lunar eclipse are below the conjunction–opposition sum, then node crossing precedes conjunction.
translations.idiomatic: Residuals below the conjunction–opposition constant mean the node is crossed before alignment.

sentences.zh: 如入交限數以上，則前會後交。

translations.literal: If they are above the node-crossing limit, then conjunction precedes node crossing.
translations.idiomatic: Values above the outer limit reverse the order: alignment happens before the node.

sentences.zh: 其前交後會近於限數者，則豫伺之；

translations.literal: When node crossing precedes conjunction and lies close to the limit number, watch ahead of time.
translations.idiomatic: Near-threshold cases with node-first geometry require advance observation.

sentences.zh: 前會後交近於限數者，則後伺之。

translations.literal: When conjunction precedes node crossing and lies close to the limit number, watch afterward.
translations.idiomatic: When conjunction leads but sits near the limit, schedule a later watch instead.

sentences.zh: 求去交度術曰：其前交後會者，今去交度分如日法而一，所得則卻交度分也。

translations.literal: Method for seeking departure from the node: for node crossing before conjunction, divide the present departure degrees and minutes by the day divisor; what is obtained is the reversed crossing degrees and minutes.
translations.idiomatic: For node-first geometry, divide the nodal residue by the day divisor to invert the crossing measure.

sentences.zh: 其前會後交者，以去交度分減會通，餘如日法而一，所得則前去交度也。

translations.literal: For conjunction before node crossing, subtract the departure degrees and minutes from the conjunction product; divide the remainder by the day divisor; what is obtained is the forward departure from the node.
translations.idiomatic: For conjunction-first geometry, subtract from 790,110 before the same division.

sentences.zh: 餘皆度分也。

translations.literal: The remainders are all in degrees and minutes.
translations.idiomatic: All such results are expressed in degrees and arc-minutes.

sentences.zh: 去交度十五以上，雖交不蝕也，十以下是蝕，十以上，虧蝕微少，光晷相及而已。

translations.literal: If the departure from the node is fifteen or more, although nodes cross there is no eclipse; if ten or less, there is an eclipse; if more than ten, the loss of light is slight, only the halos touching one another.
translations.idiomatic: Nodal distances of fifteen parts or more preclude eclipse; ten or below guarantee one; between ten and fifteen yields only a grazing penumbra.

sentences.zh: 虧之多少，以十五為法。

translations.literal: How much is lost is reckoned with fifteen as the divisor.
translations.idiomatic: Eclipse magnitude scales proportionally to fifteen as the full unit.

sentences.zh: 求日蝕虧起角術曰：其月在外道，先交後會者，虧蝕西南角起；

translations.literal: Method for seeking where a solar eclipse begins to wane from the corner: if the month is on the outer path and node crossing precedes conjunction, the waning begins from the southwest corner.
translations.idiomatic: With the moon north of the ecliptic and the node crossed before alignment, the solar bite opens in the southwest.

sentences.zh: 先會後交者，虧蝕東南角起。

translations.literal: If conjunction precedes node crossing, the waning begins from the southeast corner.
translations.idiomatic: If alignment leads the node while outside, the bite starts southeast.

sentences.zh: 其月在內道，先交後會者，虧蝕西北角起；

translations.literal: If the month is on the inner path and node crossing precedes conjunction, the waning begins from the northwest corner.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the ecliptic with node first, the darkening starts in the northwest.

sentences.zh: 先會後交者，虧蝕東北角起。

translations.literal: If conjunction precedes node crossing, the waning begins from the northeast corner.
translations.idiomatic: Inside with conjunction first, the bite opens northeast.

sentences.zh: 虧蝕分多少，如上以十五為法。

translations.literal: How much the waning amounts to is as above, using fifteen as the divisor.
translations.idiomatic: Magnitude rules mirror the fifteen-part scale used for lunar eclipses.

sentences.zh: 會交中者，蝕盡。

translations.literal: When crossing meets the midpoint, the eclipse is total.
translations.idiomatic: A central crossing yields totality.

sentences.zh: 月蝕在日之沖，虧角與上反也。

translations.literal: A lunar eclipse lies opposite the sun; the corners of loss are the reverse of the above.
translations.idiomatic: Lunar eclipses occur at the anti-sun point, so the umbral direction mirrors the solar case.

sentences.zh: 推合朔交會月蝕入遲疾曆術曰：置所入紀朔積分，以所入紀下遲疾差率數加之，以通周去之，余滿日法得一日，不盡為日餘，命日算外，則所求年天正十一月合朔入曆日也。

translations.literal: Method for pushing conjunction, node crossing, and lunar eclipse into the fast-slow calendar: set the accumulated new-moon fraction for the cycle entered, add the fast-slow difference rate listed under that cycle, remove multiples of the passage cycle; what fills the day divisor becomes one day, what does not exhaust is the day remainder; count days outside the reckoning: this is the day entered into the fast-slow table at the eleventh month’s conjunction of the year sought.
translations.idiomatic: To place a lunation inside the lunar speed table: add the tabulated anomaly increment to the lunation fraction, reduce modulo 125,621, divide by 4,559 for whole days plus remainder.

sentences.zh: 求次月，加一日，日餘四千四百五十。

translations.literal: To seek the next month, add one day, day remainder 4450.
translations.idiomatic: For the following month add one day and 4,450 day-fraction parts.

sentences.zh: 求望，加十四日，日餘三千四百八十九。

translations.literal: To seek full moon, add fourteen days, day remainder 3489.
translations.idiomatic: For opposition add fourteen days and 3,489 fractional parts.

sentences.zh: 日余滿日法成日，日滿二十七去之。

translations.literal: When day remainders fill the day divisor, they form a day; when days fill twenty-seven, remove them.
translations.idiomatic: Carry fractions into days at 4,559, then reduce full weeks of 27 days.

sentences.zh: 又除余如周日余，日餘不足除者，減一日，加周虛。

translations.literal: Again remove the remainder as with the cycle-day remainder; if day remainder is insufficient for the division, subtract one day and add the cycle shortfall.
translations.idiomatic: If the fractional division underflows, borrow one day and add the weekly complement 2,031.

sentences.zh: 推合朔交會月蝕定大小餘：以入曆日餘乘所入曆損益率，以損益盈縮積分，為定積分。

translations.literal: Method for fixing large and small remainders for conjunction, node crossing, and lunar eclipse: multiply the day remainder entered in the table by the damage-benefit rate for that entry, and with it damage or benefit the surplus-shrinkage accumulated parts, obtaining the fixed accumulated parts.
translations.idiomatic: Correct conjunction times by multiplying the anomalistic day fraction by the tabulated rate and applying it to the surplus/deficit column.

sentences.zh: 以章歲減所入曆月行分，餘以除之，所得以盈減縮加本小餘。

translations.literal: Subtract from cycle years the lunar motion parts entered in the table; divide the remainder into it; what is obtained, subtract from surplus or add to shrinkage the original small remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Divide the adjusted integral by the difference between 19 and the tabulated motion to update the fractional day.

sentences.zh: 加之滿日法者，交會加時在後日；

translations.literal: If adding fills the day divisor, the conjunction or crossing hour falls on the following day.
translations.idiomatic: A carry past the day divisor pushes the event into the next civil day.

sentences.zh: 減之不足者，交會加時在前日。

translations.literal: If subtracting is insufficient, the conjunction or crossing hour falls on the preceding day.
translations.idiomatic: A borrow moves the corrected instant onto the previous day.

sentences.zh: 月蝕者，隨定大小餘為日加時。

translations.literal: For lunar eclipses, follow the fixed large and small remainders as the day’s double-hour.
translations.idiomatic: Lunar eclipses take their clock time directly from the corrected remainder line.

sentences.zh: 入曆在周日者，以周日日餘乘縮積分，為定積分。

translations.literal: If entry falls on the cycle day, multiply shrinkage accumulated parts by the cycle-day remainder to obtain fixed accumulated parts.
translations.idiomatic: At the anomalistic week boundary, multiply the deficit column by the weekly fractional day.

sentences.zh: 以損率乘入曆日餘，又以周日日餘乘之，以周日日度小分並之，以損定積分，餘為後定積分。

translations.literal: Multiply the damage rate by the day remainder entered in the table, again multiply by the cycle-day remainder, add the cycle-day degree small fraction, and with them damage the fixed accumulated parts; the remainder is the later fixed accumulated parts.
translations.idiomatic: Combine rate products and weekly micro-parts to obtain the post-boundary correction.

sentences.zh: 以章歲減周日月行分，余以周日日餘乘之，以周日度小分並之，以除後定積分，所得以加本小餘，如上法。

translations.literal: Subtract from cycle years the moon’s motion parts for the cycle week; multiply the remainder by the cycle-day remainder, add the cycle-week degree small fraction, divide into the later fixed accumulated parts; what is obtained, add to the original small remainder, as in the method above.
translations.idiomatic: Finish the week-crossing correction by dividing the adjusted stack with the prescribed divisor mix, then add to the base fraction.

sentences.zh: 推加時：以十二乘定小餘，滿日法得一辰，數從子起，算外，則朔望加時所在辰也。

sentences.zh: 有餘不盡者四之，如日法而一為少，二為半，三為太。

translations.literal: If there is remainder not exhausted, quadruple it; divide by the day divisor to obtain shao, two makes ban, three makes tai.

sentences.zh: 又有餘者三之，如日法而一為強，半法以上排成之，不滿半法廢棄之。

translations.literal: If again there is remainder, triple it; divide by the day divisor to obtain qiang; if it fills half the divisor or more, advance it one notch; if it does not fill half the divisor, discard it.
translations.idiomatic: Further triple the tail to reach the “strong” step, rounding up at half-divisor.

sentences.zh: 以強並少為少強，並半為半強，並太為太強。

translations.literal: Combine qiang with shao to make shao-qiang; combine with ban to make ban-qiang; combine with tai to make tai-qiang.
translations.idiomatic: Add strong units to weak, half, or full subdivisions per the classical clepsydra notation.

sentences.zh: 得二強者為少弱，以之並少為半弱，以之並半為太弱，以之並太為一辰弱。

translations.literal: Obtaining two qiang makes shao-ruo; with it combine shao to make ban-ruo; with it combine ban to make tai-ruo; with it combine tai to make one chen-ruo.
translations.idiomatic: Two strongs collapse into a weak grade, stepping through the ladder to a full “weak” double-hour mark.

sentences.zh: 以所在辰命之，則各得其少、太、半及強，弱也。

translations.literal: Count by the chen where it stands, and each obtains its shao, tai, ban, and qiang, ruo.
translations.idiomatic: Read the final label against the stem hour to recover shao/tai/ban/qiang/ruo.

sentences.zh: 其月蝕望在中節前後四日以還者，視限數；

sentences.zh: 在中節前後五日以上者，視間限。

translations.idiomatic: Beyond five days from the major term, apply the wider gap-limit rule.

sentences.zh: 定小餘如間限、限數以下者，以算上為日。

sentences.zh: 中星以日所在為正，置所求年二十四氣小餘，四之，如法得一為少；

translations.idiomatic: Triple the leftover after the shao step to reach the qiang subdivision.

translations.idiomatic: Subtract those fine parts from the tabulated dusk and dawn culminations to fix each term’s reference star.

sentences.zh: 五星者，木曰歲星，火曰熒惑星，土曰填星，金曰太白星，水曰辰星。

translations.literal: The five planets: wood is called the Year Star, fire is called the Sparkling Deluder, earth is called the Filler Star, metal is called Great White, water is called the Chronogram Star.
translations.idiomatic: The five wanderers are Jupiter, Mars, Saturn, Venus, and Mercury under their classical names.

sentences.zh: 凡五星之行，有遲有疾，有留有逆。

translations.literal: Generally the motion of the five planets has slow and fast, stationing and retrograde.
translations.idiomatic: Each planet alternates between slow direct motion, fast motion, halts, and retrogrades.

sentences.zh: 曩自開闢，清濁始分，則日月五星聚于星紀。

translations.literal: Long ago, when the world first opened and clear and turbid first separated, sun, moon, and five planets gathered in the Star chronogram lodge.
translations.idiomatic: At creation’s dawn, when heaven and earth cleaved apart, the luminaries stacked together in the *Xingji* asterism.

sentences.zh: 發自星紀，並而行天，遲疾留逆，互相逮及。

translations.literal: Issuing from Star chronogram, together they course the sky, slow, fast, stationing, and retrograde mutually overtaking one another.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving that knot, they share the sky, overtaking one another through every kinematic phase.

sentences.zh: 星與日會，同宿共度，則謂之合。

translations.literal: When a star meets the sun, sharing a lodge and traversing the same degrees, it is called a conjunction.
translations.idiomatic: A planetary conjunction means the planet shares the sun’s lodge and longitude.

sentences.zh: 從合至合之日，則謂之終。

translations.literal: The days from conjunction to conjunction are called a termination.
translations.idiomatic: One synodic period runs from one conjunction to the next.

sentences.zh: 各一以終之日與一歲之日通分相約，終而率之，歲數歲則謂之合終歲數，歲終則謂之合終合數。

translations.literal: Each, with one termination’s days and one year’s days reduced by common fractions and simplified, yields a rate; the yearly number is called conjunctions per year, the termination number conjunctions per cycle.
translations.idiomatic: Reduce synodic days against the civil year to derive the mean conjunction rate and cycle count.

sentences.zh: 二率既定，則法數生焉。

translations.literal: Once the two rates are fixed, the model numbers arise from them.
translations.idiomatic: Those two ratios generate every divisor used below.

sentences.zh: 以章歲乘合數，為合月法。

translations.literal: Multiply cycle years by conjunction number to obtain the conjunction-month divisor.
translations.idiomatic: The conjunction-month divisor equals 19 times the cycle conjunction count.

sentences.zh: 以紀法乘合數，為日度法。

translations.literal: Multiply the cycle divisor by conjunction number to obtain the day-degree divisor.
translations.idiomatic: The day-degree divisor is 1,843 times the conjunction count.

sentences.zh: 以章月乘歲數，為合月分；

translations.literal: Multiply cycle months by year number to obtain conjunction-month parts.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply 235 by the synodic year count for the fractional-month numerator.

sentences.zh: 如合月法為合月數，合月之余為月餘。

translations.literal: Divide by the conjunction-month divisor for conjunction month count; the remainder of conjunction months is month remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Divide that product by the conjunction-month divisor for whole months plus a remainder.

sentences.zh: 以通數乘合月數，如日法而一，為大餘。

translations.literal: Multiply conjunction month count by the common multiple; divide by the day divisor for the large remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Scale month count by 134,630 and divide by 4,559 for the sexagenary day line.

sentences.zh: 以六十去大餘，餘為星合朔大餘。

translations.literal: Remove sixties from the large remainder; the remainder is the planet’s conjunction large remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Modulo sixty leaves the planetary conjunction day index.

sentences.zh: 大餘之餘為朔小餘。

translations.literal: The remainder of the large remainder is the new-moon small remainder.
translations.idiomatic: What remains after removing sexagenary cycles is the fractional new moon.

sentences.zh: 以通數乘月餘，以合月法乘朔小餘，並之，以日法乘合月法除之，所得星合入月日數也。

translations.literal: Multiply month remainder by the common multiple, multiply new-moon small remainder by the conjunction-month divisor, combine them, divide by the day divisor times the conjunction-month divisor; what is obtained is the days within the month when the planet conjoins.
translations.idiomatic: Combine fractional month and fractional day terms to learn how deep into the month the conjunction falls.

sentences.zh: 餘以通法約之，為入月日餘。

translations.literal: The remainder, reduced by the passage divisor, is the day remainder within the month.
translations.idiomatic: Reduce the leftover with divisor 47 for the intramonth fraction.

sentences.zh: 以朔小餘減日法，餘為朔虛分。

translations.literal: Subtract new-moon small remainder from the day divisor; the remainder is the new-moon void fraction.
translations.idiomatic: The gap to a full day divisor is the void fraction at conjunction.

sentences.zh: 以曆斗分乘合數，為星度斗分。

translations.literal: Multiply dipper fraction by conjunction number to obtain the planet’s dipper fraction in degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply the tabulated dipper part 455 by the conjunction count for arc fine structure.

sentences.zh: 木、火、土各以合數減歲數，余以周天乘之，如日度法而一，所得則行星度數也，余則度餘。

translations.literal: For wood, fire, and earth, each subtract conjunction number from year number; multiply the remainder by the full circle and divide by the day-degree divisor; what is obtained is the planet’s degree count, the remainder is degree remainder.
translations.idiomatic: For superior planets subtract synodic cycles from years, scale by 673,150, divide by the day-degree divisor.

translations.idiomatic: For inferior planets multiply years by the full revolution and divide by the same day-degree divisor.
