sentences.zh: 入月日，二十八。

translations.literal: Days entered in month, twenty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: Mercury appears on the twenty-eighth day.

sentences.zh: 日餘，二千三十四萬四千二百六十一。

translations.literal: Day remainder, 20,344,261.
translations.idiomatic: Day remainder: 20,344,261.

sentences.zh: 朔虛分，二千一百四十。

translations.literal: New-moon void fraction, 2140.
translations.idiomatic: Void fraction: 2,140.

sentences.zh: 斗分，五百三十六萬三千九百九十五。

translations.literal: Dipper fraction, 5,363,995.
translations.idiomatic: Dipper fine arc: 5,363,995.

sentences.zh: 行星度，五十七。

translations.literal: Planet degree count, fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: Arc count: fifty-seven degrees.

sentences.zh: 度餘，二千三十四萬千三百六十一。

translations.literal: Degree remainder, two thousand thirty-four myriad one thousand three hundred sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: Degree remainder aligns with the parallel day line at 20,344,261 parts.

sentences.zh: 推五星術曰：置壬辰元以來盡所求年，以合終合數乘之，滿合終歲數得一，名積合，不盡名為合餘。

translations.literal: The method for pushing the five planets says: set from the *gengchen* origin through the year sought, multiply by conjunctions per cycle; what fills conjunctions per year counts as one, named accumulated conjunctions; what does not exhaust is conjunction remainder.
translations.idiomatic: To count synodic events since the epoch: multiply years by conjunctions per cycle and divide by conjunctions per year for the quotient and remainder.

sentences.zh: 以合終合數減合餘，得一者星合往年，得二者合前往年，無所得，合其年。

translations.literal: Subtract conjunctions per cycle from conjunction remainder; obtaining one means the star conjoined in the previous year, obtaining two means it conjoined two years before; obtaining none means it conjoins in the present year.
translations.idiomatic: Compare the remainder to the cycle length to tell whether the latest conjunction fell this year or one or two years earlier.

sentences.zh: 餘以減合終合數，為度分。

translations.literal: Subtract the remainder from conjunctions per cycle to obtain degrees and parts.
translations.idiomatic: The complement of that remainder yields the arc still to complete the synodic template.

sentences.zh: 金、水積合，偶為晨，奇為夕。

translations.literal: For Venus and Mercury accumulated conjunctions, even means morning, odd means evening.
translations.idiomatic: Inferior planets alternate dawn appearances on even counts and dusk appearances on odd counts.

sentences.zh: 推五星合月：以月數、月餘各乘積合，余滿合月法從月，為積月，不盡為月餘。

translations.literal: To push the five planets’ conjunction month: multiply month count and month remainder each by accumulated conjunctions; when remainders fill the conjunction-month divisor, carry to months, obtaining accumulated months; what does not exhaust is month remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Scale the tabulated month numerator and denominator by the accumulated conjunction index.

sentences.zh: 以紀月除積月，所得算外，所入紀也，余為入紀月。

translations.literal: Divide accumulated months by cycle months; the obtained count outside the division is which cycle you entered, the remainder is months entered within the cycle.
translations.idiomatic: Divide by 22,795 to learn the cycle index and intra-cycle month offset.

sentences.zh: 副以章閏乘之，滿章月得一為閏，以減入紀月，餘以歲中去之，餘為入歲月，命以天正起，算外，星合月也。

translations.literal: In duplicate multiply by intercalations per cycle; what fills cycle months obtains one intercalation; subtract from months entered in the cycle; remove what fills a civil year from the remainder; the remainder is months entered in the year; count from the celestial-standard first month, outside the reckoning: this is the month of planetary conjunction.
translations.idiomatic: Apply the seven-in-nineteen leap rule, strip full civil years, and read the month from the winter count.

sentences.zh: 其在閏交際，以朔禦之。

translations.literal: If it lies on a leap boundary, control it with the new moon.
translations.idiomatic: At leap junctions anchor the count to the nearest conjunction rule.

sentences.zh: 推合月朔：以通數乘入紀月，滿日法得一，為積日，不盡為小餘。

translations.literal: To push conjunction new moon: multiply months entered in the cycle by the common multiple; what fills the day divisor becomes one day, what does not exhaust is the small remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Convert intra-cycle months to days with factor 134,630 ÷ 4,559.

sentences.zh: 以六十去積日，余為大餘，命以所入紀，算外，星合朔日也。

translations.literal: Remove sixties from accumulated days; the remainder is the large remainder; count by the cycle entered, outside the reckoning: this is the day of planetary conjunction.
translations.idiomatic: Modulo sixty names the conjunction’s sexagenary day.

sentences.zh: 推入月日：以通數乘月餘，合月法乘朔小餘，並之，通法約之，所得滿日度法得一，則星合入月日也，不滿日餘。

translations.literal: To push days entered in the month: multiply month remainder by the common multiple, multiply new-moon small remainder by the conjunction-month divisor, combine them, reduce by the passage divisor; what fills the day-degree divisor becomes one day, else it is day remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Blend fractional month and day terms, reduce by 47, then divide by the planet’s day-degree divisor.

sentences.zh: 命日以朔，算外，入月日也。

translations.literal: Count days by the new moon, outside the reckoning: this is the day entered in the month.
translations.idiomatic: Index the result from conjunction to mark the day within the lunation.

sentences.zh: 推星合度：以周天乘度分，滿日度法得一為度，不盡為餘。

translations.literal: To push the planet’s conjunction longitude: multiply the full circle by degree parts; what fills the day-degree divisor becomes one degree, what does not exhaust is remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply the arc template by 673,150 and divide by the day-degree divisor.

sentences.zh: 命以牛前五度起，算外，星所合度也。

translations.literal: Count from five degrees ahead of Ox, outside the reckoning: this is the degree where the planet conjoins.
translations.idiomatic: Step the result through the lodge system beginning five degrees before Ox.

sentences.zh: 求後全月：以月數加入歲月，以余加月餘，余滿合月法得一月。

translations.literal: To seek the later full month: add month count to months entered in the year, add remainder to month remainder; when remainder fills the conjunction-month divisor, obtain one month.
translations.idiomatic: Advance month tallies and carry at the conjunction-month divisor.

sentences.zh: 月不滿歲中，即在其年；

translations.literal: If months do not fill a civil year, then it lies in that year.
translations.idiomatic: A sub-year month count keeps the event inside the current year.

sentences.zh: 滿去之，有閏計焉，餘為後年；

translations.literal: If it fills, remove it; if there is an intercalation to reckon, the remainder belongs to a later year.
translations.idiomatic: Overflow past twelve civil months pushes the conjunction into the next year, with leap adjustments noted.

sentences.zh: 再滿，在後二年。

translations.literal: If it fills twice, it lies in the second following year.
translations.idiomatic: Two full overflows place the event two years ahead.

sentences.zh: 金、水加晨得夕，加夕得晨也。

translations.literal: For Venus and Mercury, add morning to obtain evening, add evening to obtain morning.
translations.idiomatic: Inferior planets flip between dawn and dusk apparitions each synodic step.

sentences.zh: 求後合朔：以朔大、小餘數加合朔月大、小餘，其月餘上成月者，又加大餘二十九，小餘二千四百一十九，小餘滿日法從大餘，命如前法。

translations.literal: To seek the later conjunction new moon: add new-moon large and small remainders to the conjunction month’s large and small remainders; if month remainders carry into a month, again add large remainder twenty-nine, small remainder 2419; when small remainder fills the day divisor, carry to large remainder; count as in the prior method.
translations.idiomatic: Propagate lunation fractions with the standard 29-day, 2,419-part increment.

sentences.zh: 求後入月日：以入月日、日餘加入月日及余，余滿日度法得一。

translations.literal: To seek later days entered in the month: add days entered and day remainders; when remainders fill the day-degree divisor, obtain one.
translations.idiomatic: Sum the intramonth lines and carry at the day-degree divisor.

sentences.zh: 其前合朔小餘滿其虛分者，去一日；

translations.literal: If the prior conjunction small remainder fills its void fraction, remove one day.
translations.idiomatic: Borrow a day when the prior void fraction is saturated.

sentences.zh: 後小餘滿二千四百一十九以上，去二十九日；

translations.literal: If the later small remainder is 2419 or more, remove twenty-nine days.
translations.idiomatic: Large fractional tails trigger a 29-day rollback.

sentences.zh: 不滿，去三十日，其餘則後合入月日，命以朔。

translations.literal: If not, remove thirty days; the remainder is the later conjunction’s day entered in the month; count by the new moon.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise subtract thirty civil days and read from conjunction.

sentences.zh: 求後合度，以度數及分，如前合宿次命之。

translations.literal: To seek the later conjunction longitude, take degree count and parts and, as with the prior conjunction, count through lodge sequence.
translations.idiomatic: Advance heliocentric longitude with the same lodge-walking rule as before.

sentences.zh: 木：晨與日合，伏，順，十六日九十九萬七千八百三十二分行星二度百七十九萬五千二百三十八分，而晨見東方，在日後。

translations.literal: Jupiter: at morning conjunction it is hidden, direct; in sixteen days and 9,978,832 parts it moves two degrees and 17,952,238 parts, then appears in the east at dawn, behind the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Jupiter’s dawn apparition opens after sixteen days plus the tabulated fraction while moving about two degrees direct while still invisible.

sentences.zh: 順，疾，日行五十七分之十一，五十七日行十一度。

translations.literal: Direct, fast, it moves eleven fifty-sevenths of a degree per day; in fifty-seven days it moves eleven degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Fast direct motion is 11/57° per day, covering 11° in fifty-seven days.

sentences.zh: 順，遲，日行九分，五十七日行九度而留。

translations.literal: Direct, slow, it moves nine fen per day; in fifty-seven days it moves nine degrees and then stations.
translations.idiomatic: Slow direct motion is 9 fen daily for fifty-seven days until station.

sentences.zh: 不行二十七日而旋。

translations.literal: It does not move for twenty-seven days, then turns.
translations.idiomatic: After a twenty-seven-day halt it turns retrograde.

sentences.zh: 逆，日行七分之一，八十四日退十二度而復留。

translations.literal: Retrograde, it moves one seventh of a degree per day; in eighty-four days it retreats twelve degrees and again stations.
translations.idiomatic: Retrograde speed is 1/7° per day, yielding 12° of retreat in eighty-four days before a second station.

sentences.zh: 二十七日復遲，日行九分，五十七日行九度而復順。

translations.literal: After twenty-seven days it again is slow, moving nine fen per day; in fifty-seven days it moves nine degrees and again is direct.
translations.idiomatic: Another twenty-seven-day pause leads back to slow direct motion at nine fen per day.

sentences.zh: 疾，日行十一分，五十七日行十一度，在日前，夕伏西方。

translations.literal: Fast, it moves eleven fen per day; in fifty-seven days it moves eleven degrees, stands before the sun, and hides at dusk in the west.
translations.idiomatic: Accelerating direct motion brings it ahead of the sun for an evening disappearance.

sentences.zh: 順，十六日九十九萬七千八百三十二分行星二度百七十九萬五千二百三十八分，而與日合。

translations.literal: Direct, in sixteen days and 9,978,832 parts it moves two degrees and 17,952,238 parts, and conjoins the sun.
translations.idiomatic: The closing hidden arc mirrors the opening sixteen-day segment before inferior conjunction.

sentences.zh: 凡一終，三百九十八日百九十九萬五千六百六十四分，行星三十三度百四十七萬二千八百六十九分。

translations.literal: In one full termination, 398 days and 199,566,664 parts, it moves thirty-three degrees and 147,286,869 parts.
translations.idiomatic: One complete synodic cycle spans 398 days plus the listed fraction and advances 33° with remainder.

sentences.zh: 火：晨與日合，伏，七十二日百七十九萬二千六百一十五分行星五十六度百二十四萬九千三百四十五分，而晨見東方，在日後。

translations.literal: Mars: at morning conjunction it is hidden, direct; in seventy-two days and 17,926,615 parts it moves fifty-six degrees and 12,493,345 parts, then appears in the east at dawn, behind the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Mars emerges after seventy-two days of direct invisibility while advancing fifty-six degrees.

sentences.zh: 順，日行二十三分之十四，百八十四日行百一十二度。

translations.literal: Direct, fast, it moves fourteen twenty-thirds of a degree per day; in one hundred eighty-four days it moves one hundred twelve degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Fast Mars averages 14/23° per day for 184 days and 112°.

sentences.zh: 更順，遲，日行十二分，九十二日行四十八度而留。

translations.literal: Again direct, slow, it moves twelve fen per day; in ninety-two days it moves forty-eight degrees and then stations.
translations.idiomatic: Slow direct motion is twelve fen daily for ninety-two days until station.

sentences.zh: 不行十一日而旋。

translations.literal: It does not move for eleven days, then turns.
translations.idiomatic: An eleven-day standstill precedes retrograde motion.

sentences.zh: 逆，日行六十二分之十七，六十二日退十七度而復留。

translations.literal: Retrograde, it moves seventeen sixty-seconds of a degree per day; in sixty-two days it retreats seventeen degrees and again stations.
translations.idiomatic: Retrograde Mars loses seventeen degrees in sixty-two days at 17/62° per day.

sentences.zh: 十一日復順，遲，日行十二分，九十二日行四十八度而復疾。

translations.literal: After eleven days it again is direct, slow, moving twelve fen per day; in ninety-two days it moves forty-eight degrees and again is fast.
translations.idiomatic: Eleven days later slow direct motion resumes, returning to fast motion after another ninety-two days.

sentences.zh: 日行十四分，百八十四日行百一十二度，在日前，夕伏西方。

translations.literal: It moves fourteen fen per day; in one hundred eighty-four days it moves one hundred twelve degrees, stands before the sun, and hides at dusk in the west.
translations.idiomatic: Fast direct motion carries it 112° in 184 days until evening invisibility.

sentences.zh: 順，七十二日百七十九萬二千六百一十五分行星五十六度百二十四萬九千三百四十五分，而與日合。

translations.literal: Direct, in seventy-two days and 17,926,615 parts it moves fifty-six degrees and 12,493,345 parts, and conjoins the sun.
translations.idiomatic: The evening arc closes with the same seventy-two-day segment as the morning opening.

sentences.zh: 凡一終，七百八十日三百五十八萬五千二百三十分，行星四百一十五度二百四十九萬八千六百九十分。

translations.literal: In one full termination, 780 days and 3,585,230 parts, it moves 415 degrees and 24,986,890 parts.
translations.idiomatic: Mars’s full synodic cycle lasts 780 days with the tabulated fractional tail and 415° of travel.

sentences.zh: 土：晨與日合，伏，十九日三百八十四萬七千六百七十五分半行星二度六百四十九萬一千一百二十一分半，而晨見東方，在日後。

translations.literal: Saturn: at morning conjunction it is hidden, direct; in nineteen days and 3,847,675.5 parts it moves two degrees and 6,491,121.5 parts, then appears in the east at dawn, behind the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Saturn’s dawn visibility follows nineteen days of tiny direct motion while still hidden.

sentences.zh: 順，行百七十二分之十三，八十六日行六度半而留。

translations.literal: Direct, it moves thirteen one hundred seventy-seconds of a degree per day; in eighty-six days it moves six and a half degrees and then stations.
translations.idiomatic: Direct Saturn creeps 13/172° per day for 86 days to a station near 6.5°.

sentences.zh: 不行三十二日半而旋。

translations.literal: It does not move for thirty-two and a half days, then turns.
translations.idiomatic: A thirty-two-and-a-half-day pause initiates retrograde motion.

sentences.zh: 逆，日行十七分之一，百二日退六度而復留。

translations.literal: Retrograde, it moves one seventeenth of a degree per day; in one hundred two days it retreats six degrees and again stations.
translations.idiomatic: Retrograde motion at 1/17° per day removes six degrees in 102 days.

sentences.zh: 不行三十二日半復順，日行十三分，八十六日行六度半，在日前，夕伏西方。

translations.literal: After not moving for thirty-two and a half days it again is direct, moving thirteen fen per day; in eighty-six days it moves six and a half degrees, stands before the sun, and hides at dusk in the west.
translations.idiomatic: The outbound arc mirrors the inbound slow direct leg before evening disappearance.

sentences.zh: 順，十九日三百八十四萬七千六百七十五分半行星二度六百四十九萬一千一百二十一分半，而與日合。

translations.literal: Direct, in nineteen days and 3,847,675.5 parts it moves two degrees and 6,491,121.5 parts, and conjoins the sun.
translations.idiomatic: The cycle closes with the same nineteen-day micro-step as at morning conjunction.

sentences.zh: 凡一終，三百七十八日六十七萬五千三百六十四分，行星十二度五百九十六萬二千二百五十六分。

translations.literal: In one full termination, 378 days and 675,364 parts, it moves twelve degrees and 5,962,256 parts.
translations.idiomatic: Saturn completes one synodic period in 378 days plus fraction, advancing only twelve degrees of sky.

sentences.zh: 金：晨與日合，伏，六日退四度，而晨見東方，在日後而逆。

translations.literal: Venus: at morning conjunction it is hidden six days, retreating four degrees, then appears in the east at dawn, behind the sun, while retrograde.
translations.idiomatic: Venus first drops four degrees in six hidden retrograde days before dawn apparition.

sentences.zh: 遲，日行五分之三，十日退六度。

translations.literal: Slow retrograde, it moves three fifths of a fen per day; in ten days it retreats six degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Slow retrograde motion removes six degrees over ten days at three fifths of a fen daily.

sentences.zh: 留，不行七日而旋。

translations.literal: It stations; for seven days it does not move, then turns.
translations.idiomatic: After a seven-day halt Venus turns from station.

sentences.zh: 順，遲，日行四十五分之三十三，四十五日行三十三度而順。

translations.literal: Direct, slow, it moves thirty-three forty-fifths of a degree per day; in forty-five days it moves thirty-three degrees and is direct.
translations.idiomatic: Slow direct motion covers 33° in forty-five days at 33/45° per day.

sentences.zh: 疾，日行一度九十一分之十四，九十一日行百五度而順。

translations.literal: Fast, it moves fourteen ninety-firsts of a degree per day; in ninety-one days it moves one hundred five degrees and is direct.
translations.idiomatic: Fast direct leg advances 105° in ninety-one days.

sentences.zh: 益疾，日行一度九十一分之二十一，九十一日行百一十二度，在日後，而晨伏東方。

translations.literal: Still faster, it moves twenty-one ninety-firsts of a degree per day; in ninety-one days it moves one hundred twelve degrees, stands behind the sun, and hides at dawn in the east.
translations.idiomatic: Peak direct speed reaches 112° before morning disappearance.

sentences.zh: 順，四十二日十九萬四千九百九十分行星五十二度十九萬四千九百九十分，而與日合。

translations.literal: Direct, in forty-two days and 1,949,990 parts it moves fifty-two degrees and 1,949,990 parts, and conjoins the sun.
translations.idiomatic: The closing direct arc lasts forty-two days plus the tabulated fraction for 52°.

sentences.zh: 一合，二百九十二日十九萬四千九百九十分，行星如之。

translations.literal: One conjunction, 292 days and 1,949,990 parts; planetary motion matches this.
translations.idiomatic: A single synodic period spans 292 days with the listed fractional tail.

sentences.zh: 金：夕與日合，伏，順，四十二日十九萬四千九百九十分行星五十二度十九萬四千九百九十分，而夕見西方，在日前。

translations.literal: Venus: at evening conjunction it is hidden, direct; in forty-two days and 1,949,990 parts it moves fifty-two degrees and 1,949,990 parts, then appears in the west at dusk, before the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Evening apparition begins after the same forty-two-day direct segment while west of the sun.

sentences.zh: 順，疾，日行一度九十一分之二十一，九十一日行百一十二度而更順。

translations.literal: Direct, fast, it moves twenty-one ninety-firsts of a degree per day; in ninety-one days it moves one hundred twelve degrees and again is direct.
translations.idiomatic: Evening fast direct motion mirrors the morning leg.

sentences.zh: 遲，日行一度十四分，九十一日行百五度而順。

translations.literal: Slow, it moves one degree and fourteen fen per day; in ninety-one days it moves one hundred five degrees and is direct.
translations.idiomatic: Slowing to one degree fourteen fen daily for ninety-one days.

sentences.zh: 益遲，日行四十五分之三十三，四十五日行三十三度而留。

translations.literal: Still slower, it moves thirty-three forty-fifths of a degree per day; in forty-five days it moves thirty-three degrees and stations.
translations.idiomatic: Final deceleration leads to station after forty-five days.

sentences.zh: 不行七日而旋。

translations.literal: For seven days it does not move, then turns.
translations.idiomatic: Another week-long standstill precedes retrograde motion.

sentences.zh: 逆，日行五分之三，十日退六度，在日前，夕伏西方。

translations.literal: Retrograde, it moves three fifths of a fen per day; in ten days it retreats six degrees, stands before the sun, and hides at dusk in the west.
translations.idiomatic: Evening retrograde removes six degrees in ten days before invisibility.

sentences.zh: 逆，六日退四度，而與日合。

translations.literal: Retrograde, in six days it retreats four degrees, and conjoins the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Six retrograde days erase four degrees down to inferior conjunction.

sentences.zh: 凡再合一終，五百八十四日三十八萬九千九百八十分，行星如之。

translations.literal: In all, two conjunctions complete one termination: 584 days and 3,899,980 parts; planetary motion matches this.
translations.idiomatic: Two synodic cycles total 584 days with the stated remainder.

sentences.zh: 水：晨與日合，伏，十一日退七度，而晨見東方，在日後。

translations.literal: Mercury: at morning conjunction it is hidden; in eleven days it retreats seven degrees, then appears in the east at dawn, behind the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Mercury’s dawn arc opens with eleven retrograde degrees.

sentences.zh: 逆，疾，一日退一度而留。

translations.literal: Retrograde, fast, it retreats one degree in one day and then stations.
translations.idiomatic: Rapid retrograde cancels a full degree in a single day before halting.

sentences.zh: 不行一日而旋。

translations.literal: For one day it does not move, then turns.
translations.idiomatic: A one-day station separates retrograde from direct motion.

sentences.zh: 順，遲，日行八分之七，八日行七度而順。

translations.literal: Direct, slow, it moves seven eighths of a fen per day; in eight days it moves seven degrees and is direct.
translations.idiomatic: Slow direct motion adds seven degrees in eight days.

sentences.zh: 疾，日行一度十八分之四，十八日行二十二度，在日後，晨伏東方。

translations.literal: Fast, it moves one degree and four eighteenths per day; in eighteen days it moves twenty-two degrees, stands behind the sun, and hides at dawn in the east.
translations.idiomatic: Accelerating direct motion reaches twenty-two degrees before morning disappearance.

sentences.zh: 順，十八日二千三十四萬四千二百六十一分行星三十六度二千三十四萬四千二百六十一分，而與日合。

translations.literal: Direct, in eighteen days and 20,344,261 parts it moves thirty-six degrees and 20,344,261 parts, and conjoins the sun.
translations.idiomatic: The hidden direct arc closes in eighteen days with the tabulated fractional degrees.

sentences.zh: 凡一合，五十七日二千三十四萬四千二百六十一分，行星如之。

translations.literal: In one conjunction, fifty-seven days and 20,344,261 parts; planetary motion matches this.
translations.idiomatic: Mercury’s synodic period is fifty-seven days plus the listed fraction.

sentences.zh: 水：夕與日合，伏，十八日二千三十四萬四千二百六十一分行星三十六度二千三十四萬四千二百六十一分，而夕見西方，在日前。

translations.literal: Mercury: at evening conjunction it is hidden; in eighteen days and 20,344,261 parts it moves thirty-six degrees and 20,344,261 parts, then appears in the west at dusk, before the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Evening apparition follows the same eighteen-day segment while east of the sun.

sentences.zh: 順，疾，日行一度十八分之四，十八日行二十二度而更順。

translations.literal: Direct, fast, it moves one degree and four eighteenths per day; in eighteen days it moves twenty-two degrees and again is direct.
translations.idiomatic: Evening fast direct motion repeats the eighteen-day pattern.

sentences.zh: 遲，日行八分之七，八日行七度而留。

translations.literal: Slow, it moves seven eighths of a fen per day; in eight days it moves seven degrees and stations.
translations.idiomatic: Deceleration ends in an eight-day station.

sentences.zh: 不行一日而旋。

translations.literal: For one day it does not move, then turns.
translations.idiomatic: A single idle day marks the retrograde pivot.

sentences.zh: 逆，一日退一度，在日前，夕伏西方。

translations.literal: Retrograde, it retreats one degree in one day, stands before the sun, and hides at dusk in the west.
translations.idiomatic: Fast retrograde erases a degree daily until evening invisibility.

sentences.zh: 逆，十一日退七度，而與日合。

translations.literal: Retrograde, in eleven days it retreats seven degrees, and conjoins the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Eleven retrograde days remove seven degrees to inferior conjunction.

sentences.zh: 凡再合一終，百一十五日千八百九十六萬一千三百九十五分，行星如之。

translations.literal: In all, two conjunctions complete one termination: 115 days and 18,961,395 parts; planetary motion matches this.
translations.idiomatic: Mercury’s double synodic cycle totals 115 days with remainder.

sentences.zh: 五星曆步術

translations.literal: Methods for pacing the five planets through the ephemeris.
translations.idiomatic: Heading: stepwise planetary computation.

sentences.zh: 以法伏日度餘加星合日度余，余滿日度法得一從全，命之如前，得星見日及度餘也。

translations.literal: Add hidden days and degree remainders to the planet’s conjunction day and degree remainders; when remainders fill the day-degree divisor, obtain one and carry to whole degrees; count as before to obtain the day of appearance and degree remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Sum the tabulated hidden arc to the conjunction line, carrying at the day-degree divisor.

sentences.zh: 以星行分母乘見度分，如日度法得一，分不盡，半法以上亦得一，而日加所行分，分滿其母得一度。

translations.literal: Multiply appearance degree parts by the planet’s motion denominator; divide by the day-degree divisor to obtain one; if parts do not exhaust, if half the divisor or more also count as one; then add the daily motion parts; when parts fill their denominator, obtain one degree.
translations.idiomatic: Convert fractional motion using each planet’s denominator with rounding at half divisor.

sentences.zh: 逆順母不同，以當行之母乘故分，如故母而一，當行分也。

translations.literal: If retrograde and direct denominators differ, multiply old parts by the active denominator and divide by the old denominator to obtain active parts.
translations.idiomatic: Rescale fractional steps whenever retrograde and direct legs use different divisors.

sentences.zh: 留者承前，逆則減之，伏不盡度，除斗分，以行母為率。

translations.literal: Stationing inherits the previous leg; retrograde subtracts it; if hidden degrees do not exhaust, remove dipper fraction, using the motion denominator as rate.
translations.idiomatic: Station lines continue prior totals; retrograde subtracts; hidden legs drop dipper fractions.

sentences.zh: 分有損益，前後相禦。

translations.literal: Parts may damage or benefit; front and rear legs control one another.
translations.idiomatic: Sequential segments borrow or lend fractional parts across the synodic table.

sentences.zh: 武帝侍中平原劉智，以鬥曆改憲，推《四分法》，三百年而減一日，以百五十為度法，三十七為斗分。

translations.literal: Attendant-in-ordinary Liu Zhi of Pingyuan, serving Emperor Wu, altered the pitch-pipe calendar with a new canon, pushed the *Quarter-Day* method, subtracting one day every three hundred years, taking one hundred fifty as the degree divisor and thirty-seven as the dipper fraction.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhi revised the calendrical constants, tightening the quarter-day system with divisor 150 and dipper fraction 37.

sentences.zh: 推甲子為上元，至泰始十年，歲在甲午，九萬七千四百一十一歲，上元天正甲子朔夜半冬至，日月五星始于星紀，得元首之端。

translations.literal: He pushed *jiazi* as high origin; down to the tenth year of Taishi, the year being *jiawu*, 97,411 years from high origin, at midnight on the celestial-standard *jiazi* new moon and winter solstice, sun, moon, and five planets began in the Star chronogram lodge, obtaining the tip of the first stem’s head.
translations.idiomatic: His epoch placed a grand conjunction of luminaries at winter solstice 274 CE minus 97,411 years.

sentences.zh: 飾以浮說，名為《正曆》。

translations.literal: He adorned it with inflated claims and titled it the *Corrected Calendar*.
translations.idiomatic: He packaged the scheme rhetorically as the *Zhengli* calendar.

sentences.zh: 當陽侯杜預著《春秋長曆》，說云：

translations.literal: Marquis Du Yu of Dangyang composed the *Extended Spring and Autumn Calendar*, remarking:
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu’s *Chunqiu Changli* prefaces a methodological note.

sentences.zh: 日行一度，月行十三度十九分之七有奇，日官當會集此之遲疾，以考成晦朔，以設閏月。

translations.literal: The sun moves one degree per day, the moon thirteen and seven nineteenths degrees with a remainder; calendar officers should collate these varying speeds to fix last and first days of months and to set intercalary months.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu urges averaging solar and lunar speeds to regulate conjunctions and intercalations.

sentences.zh: 閏月無中氣，而北斗邪指兩辰之間，所以異於他月。

translations.literal: An intercalary month lacks a mid-climate, and the Dipper skews between two stems—how it differs from other months.
translations.idiomatic: Leap months sit without major qi while the Dipper handle straddles two celestial positions.

sentences.zh: 積此以相通，四時八節無違，乃得成歲，其微密至矣。

translations.literal: Accumulating these rules keeps the four seasons and eight nodes without error, completing the year; the fineness is extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Stacking such checks preserves the agrarian year with maximal precision.

sentences.zh: 得其精微，以合天道，則事敘而不愆。

translations.literal: Grasping that fineness to match the Way of Heaven orders affairs without fault.
translations.idiomatic: Matching heaven’s subtle ticks keeps human schedules aligned.

sentences.zh: 故《傳》曰：「閏以正時，時以作事。

translations.literal: Therefore the *Zuo Tradition* says: “Intercalations rectify the seasons; seasons enable work.”
translations.idiomatic: Hence the classic line that leap months fix seasons and seasons shape labor.

sentences.zh: 」然陰陽之運，隨動而差，差而不已，遂與曆錯。

translations.literal: Yet the courses of yin and yang shift as they move; once they shift without end, they eventually disagree with the calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Natural drift means any fixed table eventually diverges from the sky.

sentences.zh: 故仲尼、丘明每于朔閏發文，蓋矯正得失，因以宣明歷數也。

translations.literal: Therefore Zhongni and Qiu Ming repeatedly wrote on new and intercalary moons to correct gains and losses and thereby clarify calendrical reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius and Zuo Qiuming foregrounded calendrical notes to expose systematic error.

sentences.zh: 劉子駿造《三正曆》以修《春秋》，日蝕有甲乙者三十四，而《三正曆》惟得一蝕，比諸家既最疏。

translations.literal: Liu Xin’s *Three Origins Calendar*, used to edit the *Spring and Autumn*, matched only one of thirty-four eclipses dated with stem-branch days, making it looser than every rival system.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xin’s scheme failed thirty-three of thirty-four dated eclipses in the annals.

sentences.zh: 又六千餘歲輒益一日，凡歲當累日為次，而故益之，此不可行之甚者。

translations.literal: Moreover, every six thousand-odd years it arbitrarily adds one day; years ought to accumulate fractional days in sequence, yet it adds them wrongly—this is among the worst unworkable flaws.
translations.idiomatic: Its long-cycle leap stole whole days without astronomical warrant.

sentences.zh: 自古已來，諸論《春秋》者多違謬，或造家術，或用黃帝已來諸曆，以推經傳朔日，皆不諧合。

translations.literal: Since antiquity, most who discoursed on the *Spring and Autumn* have erred, inventing private methods or applying calendars from the Yellow Emperor onward to compute Classic and Commentary new-moon days, none of which harmonize.
translations.idiomatic: Later scholars forced mismatched epochal calendars onto the *Chunqiu* text.

sentences.zh: 日蝕於朔，此乃天驗，《經傳》又書其朔蝕，可謂得天，而劉賈諸儒說，皆以為月二日或三日，公違聖人明文，其弊在於守一元，不與天消息也。

translations.literal: Solar eclipses fall on new moons—Heaven itself attests this, and the Classic and Commentary record conjunction eclipses, so they match Heaven; yet Liu, Jia, and other exegetes insist on the second or third day of the month, openly contradicting the sages’ explicit wording—the fault lies in clinging to one origin without tracking Heaven’s message.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu faults commentators who moved eclipses off conjunction to save flawed calendars.

sentences.zh: 餘感《春秋》之事，嘗著《曆論》，極言曆之通理。

translations.literal: Stirred by these *Spring and Autumn* issues, I once wrote a *Discourse on Calendars* that exhausts the general principles of reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu authored a calendar treatise to defend conjunction-based interpretation.

sentences.zh: 其大指曰：「天行不息，日月星辰各運其舍，皆動物也。

translations.literal: Its main point says: “Heaven’s motion never rests; sun, moon, and asterisms each run their lodges—they are all moving things.”
translations.idiomatic: Heaven’s bodies are in constant motion, each wheeling through its mansions.

sentences.zh: 物動則不一，雖行度有大量可得而限，累日為月，累月為歲，以新故相涉，不得不有毫末之差，此自然之理也。

translations.literal: When things move they are not uniform; although their tracks have broad measures that can be bounded, stacking days into months and months into years means old and new phases overlap and cannot lack hair’s-breadth discrepancies—this is the pattern of nature.
translations.idiomatic: Discrete month-year stacking inevitably accumulates tiny drift.

sentences.zh: 故春秋日有頻月而蝕者，有曠年不蝕者，理不得一，而算守恆數，故曆無不有先後也。

translations.literal: Therefore in the *Spring and Autumn* months sometimes eclipse repeatedly while years sometimes pass without eclipse; principle cannot be uniform, yet computation clings to fixed numbers, so calendars always disagree sooner or later.
translations.idiomatic: Eclipse frequency varies, so rigid constants must eventually fail.

sentences.zh: 始失於毫毛，而尚未可覺，積而成多，以失弦望晦朔，則不得不改憲以從之。

translations.literal: Error begins smaller than a hair and is still imperceptible, yet accumulating it misses quarters, full moons, dark and bright days, forcing one to reform the canon to follow Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Neglected fractions snowball until only calendar reform recovers conjunctions.

sentences.zh: 《書》所謂「欽若昊天，曆象日月星辰」，《易》所謂「治曆明時」，言當順天以求合，非為合以驗天者也。

translations.literal: What the *Documents* calls “revere and accord with august Heaven, sequence sun, moon, and asterisms,” and what the *Changes* calls “regulate the calendar and clarify the seasons,” means one should follow Heaven to seek agreement, not twist Heaven to vindicate a scheme.
translations.idiomatic: Classical dicta demand fitting the calendar to the sky, not the reverse.

sentences.zh: 推此論之，春秋二百餘年，其治曆變通多矣。

translations.literal: Pushing this argument across the more than two hundred years of the *Spring and Autumn*, calendrical practice shifted many times.
translations.idiomatic: Lu state’s methods evolved across the *Chunqiu* centuries.

sentences.zh: 雖數術絕滅，遠尋《經傳》微旨，大量可知，時之違謬，則《經傳》有驗。

translations.literal: Although numerical arts are lost, probing the subtle wording of Classic and Commentary still reveals the broad pattern: wherever timing errs, the texts themselves supply checks.
translations.idiomatic: Internal textual evidence exposes which calendars fit which reigns.

sentences.zh: 學者固當曲循《經傳》月日、日蝕，以考晦朔，以推時驗；

translations.literal: Students ought meekly follow Classic and Commentary month-days and eclipse records to test dark and bright days and verify seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars should privilege manuscript dates over private algorithms.

sentences.zh: 而皆不然，各據其學，以推春秋，此無異於度己之跡，而欲削他人之足也。

translations.literal: Yet none do so; each presses his own school onto the *Spring and Autumn*—no different from measuring one’s own footprint to chop another’s foot.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu likens partisan calendar claims to self-referential violence.

sentences.zh: 餘為《曆論》之後，至咸寧中，善算者李修、卜顯，依論體為術，名《乾度曆》，表上朝廷。

translations.literal: After I wrote the *Discourse on Calendars*, by the Xianning era skilled calculators Li Xiu and Bu Xian, following its framework, devised a method titled the *Qian Du Calendar* and presented it at court.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiu and Bu Xian codified Du Yu’s ideas as the *Qiandu* system.

sentences.zh: 其術合日行四分數而微增月行，用三百歲改憲之意，二元相推，七十餘歲，承以強弱，強弱之差蓋少，而適足以遠通盈縮。

translations.literal: Their method matched the sun’s daily quarter fraction while slightly increasing the moon’s motion, using the idea of reforming the canon every three hundred years; the two origins interact over seventy-odd years through strength and weakness; the strength–weakness gap is small yet just enough to span expansions and contractions over long spans.
translations.idiomatic: The *Qiandu* scheme layered gentle solar-lunar tweaks across linked epochs.

sentences.zh: 時尚書及史官，以《乾度》與《泰始曆》參校古今記注，《乾度曆》殊勝《泰始曆》，上勝官曆四十五事。

translations.literal: Then the Director of the Secretariat and clerks compared *Qiandu* with the *Taishi* calendar against ancient and modern records; *Qiandu* surpassed *Taishi* overall, winning forty-five points against the official calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Court validation favored *Qiandu* in forty-five head-to-head tests.

sentences.zh: 今其術具存。

translations.literal: Today its method still survives intact.
translations.idiomatic: The *Qiandu* algorithm remains fully documented.

sentences.zh: 又並考古今十曆以驗《春秋》，知《三統》之最疏也。

translations.literal: They also collated ten calendars ancient and modern against the *Spring and Autumn*, showing the *Triple Concordance* to be the loosest.
translations.idiomatic: Comparative testing ranked Liu Xin’s *San tong* worst.

sentences.zh: 《春秋》大凡七百七十九日，三百九十三《經》，三百八十六《傳》。

translations.literal: The *Spring and Autumn* altogether spans 779 days: 393 in the Classic, 386 in the Commentary.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu counts 779 dated lines split between text and *Zuo*.

sentences.zh: 其三十七日食。

translations.literal: Of these, thirty-seven record eclipses.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty-seven lines note solar eclipses.

sentences.zh: 三無甲乙。

translations.literal: Three lack stem-branch tags.
translations.idiomatic: Three eclipse entries omit the sexagenary day.

sentences.zh: 《黃帝》曆得四百六十六日，一蝕。

translations.literal: The *Yellow Emperor* calendar yields 466 days, one eclipse match.
translations.idiomatic: The Huangdi table aligns only one eclipse in 466 test days.

sentences.zh: 《顓頊曆》得五百九日，八蝕。

translations.literal: The *Zhuanxu* calendar yields 509 days, eight eclipse matches.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhuanxu scheme scores eight hits in 509 days.

sentences.zh: 《夏曆》得五百三十六日，十四蝕。

translations.literal: The *Xia* calendar yields 536 days, fourteen eclipse matches.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia calendar nets fourteen hits over 536 days.

sentences.zh: 《真夏曆》得四百六十六日，一蝕。

translations.literal: The *True Xia* calendar yields 466 days, one eclipse match.
translations.idiomatic: The revised Xia table matches one eclipse.

sentences.zh: 《殷曆》得五百三日，十三蝕。

translations.literal: The *Yin* calendar yields 503 days, thirteen eclipse matches.
translations.idiomatic: The Yin calendar scores thirteen hits in 503 days.

sentences.zh: 《周曆》得五百六日，十三蝕。

translations.literal: The *Zhou* calendar yields 506 days, thirteen eclipse matches.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou calendar yields thirteen hits in 506 days.

sentences.zh: 《真周曆》得四百八十五日，一蝕。

translations.literal: The *True Zhou* calendar yields 485 days, one eclipse match.
translations.idiomatic: The refined Zhou line scores one hit.

sentences.zh: 《魯曆》得五百二十九日，十三蝕。

translations.literal: The *Lu* calendar yields 529 days, thirteen eclipse matches.
translations.idiomatic: Lu’s official calendar scores thirteen hits in 529 days.

sentences.zh: 《三統曆》得四百八十四日，一蝕。

translations.literal: The *Triple Concordance* calendar yields 484 days, one eclipse match.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xin’s system manages one hit in 484 days.

sentences.zh: 《乾象曆》得四百九十五日，七蝕。

translations.literal: The *Qianxiang* calendar yields 495 days, seven eclipse matches.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hong’s *Qianxiang* scores seven hits in 495 days.

sentences.zh: 《泰始曆》得五百一十日，十九蝕。

translations.literal: The *Taishi* calendar yields 510 days, nineteen eclipse matches.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin *Taishi* calendar reaches nineteen hits in 510 days.

sentences.zh: 《乾度曆》得五百三十八日，十九蝕。

translations.literal: The *Qiandu* calendar yields 538 days, nineteen eclipse matches.
translations.idiomatic: *Qiandu* edges slightly ahead with nineteen hits in 538 days.

sentences.zh: 今《長曆》得七百四十六日，三十三蝕。

translations.literal: Du Yu’s present *Extended Calendar* yields 746 days, thirty-three eclipse matches.
translations.idiomatic: Du’s own reconstruction scores thirty-three hits across 746 days.

sentences.zh: 失三十三日，《經傳》誤；

translations.literal: It misses thirty-three days because Classic and Commentary are mistaken.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty-three day mismatches stem from textual corruption, not the model.

sentences.zh: 四日蝕，三無甲乙。

translations.literal: Four eclipse records lack true conjunction; three omit stems and branches.
translations.idiomatic: Four eclipses are misdated; three entries lack sexagenary tags.

sentences.zh: 漢末，宋仲子集七曆以考《春秋》，案其夏、周二曆術數，皆與《藝文志》所記不同，故更名為《真夏》、《真周曆》也。

translations.literal: Late Han, Song Zhongzi collated seven calendars to test the *Spring and Autumn*; inspecting Xia and Zhou algorithms showed they differed from the *Bibliographic Treatise*, so he renamed them *True Xia* and *True Zhou*.
translations.idiomatic: Song Zhongzi distinguished authentic Xia and Zhou reconstructions from Han catalogue versions.

sentences.zh: 穆帝永和八年，著作郎琅邪王朔之造《通曆》，以甲子為上元，積九萬七千年，四千八百八十三為紀法，千二百五為斗分，因其上元為開闢之始。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yonghe under Emperor Mu, Wang Shuozhi, editorial director from Langya, made the *Comprehensive Calendar*, taking *jiazi* as high origin, accumulating ninety-seven thousand years, with 4,883 as cycle divisor and 1,205 as dipper fraction, treating that origin as the opening of creation.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shuozhi’s *Tongli* used a mythic deep epoch with custom divisors.

sentences.zh: 後秦姚興時，當孝武太元九年，歲在甲申，天水姜岌造《三紀甲子元曆》，其略曰：「治曆之道，必審日月之行，然後可以上考天時，下察地化。

translations.literal: Under Later Qin’s Yao Xing, in the ninth year of Taiyuan of Emperor Xiaowu, the year being *jiashen*, Jiang Ji of Tianshui composed the *Three Eras Jiazi Origin Calendar*, stating in summary: “The way of regulating calendars must scrutinize the courses of sun and moon, then one can investigate heavenly seasons above and inspect earthly transformations below.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Ji’s preface stresses observing sun and moon before tuning the civil year.

sentences.zh: 一失其本，則四時變移。

translations.literal: Once their root is lost, the four seasons shift.
translations.idiomatic: If solar and lunar roots err, seasonal markers wander.

sentences.zh: 故仲尼之作《春秋》，日以繼月，月以繼時，時以繼年，年以首事，明天時者人事之本，是以王者重之。

translations.literal: Therefore when Zhongni composed the *Spring and Autumn*, days follow months, months follow seasons, seasons follow years, and years head affairs, showing that clarifying heavenly seasons is the root of human affairs—hence kings prize it.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius chained day-month-season-year to show royal governance depends on heaven’s timetable.

sentences.zh: 自皇羲以降，暨于漢魏，各自製曆，以求厥中。

translations.literal: From august Xi downward to Han and Wei, each age fashioned its own calendar to seek the mean.
translations.idiomatic: Every dynasty revised constants to chase the celestial middle.

sentences.zh: 考其疏密，惟交會薄蝕可以驗之。

translations.literal: Testing their looseness or tightness, only node crossings and thin eclipses can verify them.
translations.idiomatic: Only conjunctions and grazing eclipses falsify or confirm a scheme.

sentences.zh: 然書契所記，惟《春秋》著日蝕之變，自隱公訖於哀公，凡二百四十二年之間，日蝕三十有六，考其晦朔，不知用何曆也。

translations.literal: Yet what written records preserve is that only the *Spring and Autumn* notes solar-eclipse anomalies; from Duke Yin to Duke Ai, across 242 years, there are thirty-six eclipses, and checking their dark and bright days shows no knowing which calendar was used.
translations.idiomatic: The *Chunqiu* eclipse set spans 242 years with thirty-six events of uncertain calendrical backing.

sentences.zh: 班固以為《春秋》因《魯曆》，《魯曆》不正，故置閏失其序。

translations.literal: Ban Gu thought the *Spring and Autumn* followed the *Lu* calendar, and that the *Lu* calendar was incorrect, so intercalations lost their order.
translations.idiomatic: Ban Gu blamed Lu’s irregular leap placement.

sentences.zh: 魯以閏餘一之歲為蔀首，檢《春秋》置閏不與此蔀相符也。

translations.literal: Lu took the year whose intercalary remainder was one as *bu* head, yet checking *Spring and Autumn* intercalations does not match that *bu*.
translations.idiomatic: Lu’s supposed leap rule fails against the annals’ actual leap months.

sentences.zh: 《命曆序》曰：孔子為治《春秋》之故，退修殷之故曆，使其數可傳於後。

translations.literal: The *Ordered Lives of Calendars* says: Confucius, to order the *Spring and Autumn*, withdrew and revised Yin’s old calendar so its numbers could transmit to later ages.
translations.idiomatic: The *Ming li xu* credits Confucius with an Yin-based editorial calendar.

sentences.zh: 如是，《春秋》宜用《殷曆》正之。

translations.literal: If so, the *Spring and Autumn* ought to be corrected with the *Yin* calendar.
translations.idiomatic: That tradition would privilege the Yin table for *Chunqiu* dates.

sentences.zh: 今考其交會，不與《殷曆》相應，以《殷曆》考《春秋》，月朔多不及其日，又以檢《經》，率多一日，《傳》率少一日。

translations.literal: Now examining its node crossings, they do not match the *Yin* calendar; testing the *Yin* calendar against the *Spring and Autumn*, month beginnings mostly fall short of recorded days; checking the Classic, it usually runs one day ahead, the Commentary usually one day short.
translations.idiomatic: Empirical checks show Yin’s conjunctions misalign with both text layers.

sentences.zh: 但《公羊》、《經》、《傳》異朔，於理可從，而《經》有蝕朔之驗，《傳》為失之也。

translations.literal: Only where *Gongyang*, Classic, and Commentary disagree on the new moon may principle follow one side, yet the Classic carries eclipse-at-conjunction verification while the Commentary errs.
translations.idiomatic: Eclipse evidence vindicates the Classic’s conjunctions over the *Zuo* variants.

sentences.zh: 服虔解《傳》用太極上元，太極上元乃《三統曆》劉歆所造元也，何緣施於《春秋》？

translations.literal: Fu Qian explained the Commentary using the Supreme Ultimate high origin—yet that Supreme Ultimate origin is the epoch Liu Xin invented for the *Triple Concordance* calendar; on what grounds apply it to the *Spring and Autumn*?
translations.idiomatic: Fu Qian’s borrowing of Liu Xin’s Han-era origin is anachronistic.

sentences.zh: 於《春秋》而用《漢曆》，於義無乃遠乎？

translations.literal: To use Han calendars on the *Spring and Autumn*—does that not stretch principle too far?
translations.idiomatic: Applying Eastern Han mathematics to Spring and Autumn chronology is historically strained.

sentences.zh: 《傳》之違失多矣，不惟斯事而已。

translations.literal: The Commentary’s errors are many, not only this matter.
translations.idiomatic: The *Zuo* text is flawed on more than calendrics alone.

sentences.zh: 襄公二十七年冬十有一月乙亥朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: Duke Xiang’s twenty-seventh year, winter, eleventh month, *yihai* new moon, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: The record cites the eleventh month’s *yihai* day, year 546 BCE, for a solar eclipse (opening a longer gloss).

sentences.zh: 《傳》曰：'辰在申，司曆過，再失閏也。

translations.literal: The Commentary says: ‘The chronogram is in *shen*; the calendar officer erred—this is doubly missing an intercalation.’
translations.idiomatic: The *Zuo* gloss: the branch mismatch shows the official calendar missed two leap insertions.

sentences.zh: '考其去交分，交會應在此月，而不為再失閏也。

translations.literal: Examining its departure-from-node fraction, the crossing ought to fall in this month, and it is not a case of doubly missing an intercalation.
translations.idiomatic: Checking the nodal residue shows the month placement is wrong, not the leap count.

sentences.zh: 案歆曆於《春秋》日蝕一朔，其餘多在二日。

translations.literal: Investigating Xin’s calendar against *Spring and Autumn* solar eclipses, one falls on new moon; the rest mostly fall on the second day.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xin’s table hits only one true conjunction eclipse; most land a day late.

sentences.zh: 因附《五行傳》，著朓與側匿之說云：春秋時諸侯多失其政，故月行恆遲。

translations.literal: Therefore he appended the *Treatise on the Five Phases*, setting forth theories of “fat” and “side concealment,” saying: in *Spring and Autumn* times the feudal lords mostly lost good government, so the moon’s motion was always slow.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xin blamed politics for systematic lunar lag instead of adjusting his fractions.

sentences.zh: 歆不以曆失天，而為之差說。

translations.literal: Xin did not treat the calendar as missing Heaven, but spun differential explanations.
translations.idiomatic: He invented moralized excuses rather than fixing constants.

sentences.zh: 日之食朔，此乃天驗也，而歆反以曆非此，冤天而負時曆也。

translations.literal: That eclipses fall on new moons is Heaven’s own verification, yet Xin claimed the calendar was not at fault—wronging Heaven and slandering timely calendars.
translations.idiomatic: Conjunction eclipses prove his model wrong, yet he impugned the sky.

sentences.zh: 杜預又以為周衰世亂，學者莫得其真，今之所傳七曆，皆未必是時王之術也。

translations.literal: Du Yu also thought that with Zhou’s decline and age’s disorder, scholars could not obtain the truth, and that none of the seven transmitted calendars need be the royal method of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu doubted any extant system truly matched Zhou court practice.

sentences.zh: 今誠以七家之曆，以考古今交會，信無其驗也，皆由斗分疏之所致也。

translations.literal: If one sincerely tests those seven houses against ancient and modern node crossings, they truly lack verification, all because the dipper fraction is too loose.
translations.idiomatic: Comparative eclipse work exposes loose dipper fractions across all seven schools.

sentences.zh: 《殷曆》以四分一為斗分，《三統》以一千五百三十九分之三百八十五為斗分，《乾象》以五百八十九分之一百四十五為斗分，今《景初》以一千八百四十三分之四百五十五為斗分，疏密不同，法數各異。

translations.literal: The *Yin* calendar took one quarter as dipper fraction; the *Triple Concordance* took 385/1539; *Qianxiang* took 145/589; the present *Jingchu* takes 455/1843: coarse and fine differ, and the model numbers diverge.
translations.idiomatic: Historical dipper fractions range from 1/4 to the *Jingchu* ratio, each implying different mean motions.

sentences.zh: 《殷曆》斗分粗，故不施於今。

translations.literal: The *Yin* dipper fraction is coarse, so it is not applied today.
translations.idiomatic: Yin’s crude quarter cannot serve modern reckoning.

sentences.zh: 《乾象》斗分細，故不得通于古。

translations.literal: The *Qianxiang* dipper fraction is fine, so it cannot extend through antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: *Qianxiang*’s tight fraction fails deep retrotests.

sentences.zh: 《景初》斗分雖在粗細之中，而日之所在乃差四度，日月虧已，皆不及其次，假使日在東井而蝕，以月驗之，乃在參六度，差違乃爾，安可以考天時人事乎？

translations.literal: Although the *Jingchu* dipper fraction lies between coarse and fine, the sun’s place still misses by four degrees; sun and moon already wax and wane yet do not reach their lodges—suppose the sun stands in Well while eclipsing: testing by the moon, it is actually near Triaster at six degrees; error is this huge—how can one thereby investigate heavenly seasons and human affairs?
translations.idiomatic: Even *Jingchu* mislocates solar longitude by several degrees, vitiating eclipse predictions.

sentences.zh: 今治新曆，以二千四百五十一分之六百五為斗分，日在鬥十七度，天正之首，上可以考合於《春秋》，下可以取驗於今世。

translations.literal: Now compiling a new calendar, we take 605/2451 as dipper fraction, the sun at seventeen degrees of Dipper at the head of the celestial-standard year: upward it can be checked against the *Spring and Autumn*, downward verified in the present age.
translations.idiomatic: The proposed 605/2451 ratio anchors the sun at 17° in Dipper at year head for dual classical and modern fit.

sentences.zh: 以之考《春秋》三十六蝕，正朔者二十有五，蝕二日者二，蝕晦者二，誤者五，凡三十三蝕，其餘蝕經無日諱之名，無以考其得失 。

translations.literal: Testing it on the *Spring and Autumn*’s thirty-six eclipses, twenty-five fall on true new moon, two on the second day, two on last day of month, five are wrong—thirty-three in all; the remaining eclipses lack dated stems in the Classic, so their success or failure cannot be checked.
translations.idiomatic: The new table scores twenty-five exact conjunctions among thirty-six, with several edge cases and five clear misses.

sentences.zh: 圖緯皆云「三百歲鬥曆改憲」。

translations.literal: Charts and weft-texts all say, ‘Every three hundred years the dipper calendar reforms the canon.’
translations.idiomatic: Apocrypha prescribe a three-century calendrical overhaul.

sentences.zh: 以今新施於春秋之世，日蝕多在朔，春秋之世，下至於今，凡一千餘歲，交會弦望故進退於三蝕之間，此法乃可永載用之，豈三百歲鬥曆改憲者乎？

translations.literal: If the present new system is applied to *Spring and Autumn* times, eclipses mostly fall on new moon; from *Spring and Autumn* down to today, over a thousand years, conjunctions and quarters still drift within three-eclipse margins—this method can be used forever; is it merely ‘every three hundred years reform the dipper calendar’?
translations.idiomatic: The author argues his scheme tracks eclipses across millennia, not just per apocryphal 300-year cycle.

sentences.zh: 然則算步究于元初，約法施於今用，曲求其趣，則各有宜，故作者兩設其法也。

translations.idiomatic: Full and abbreviated planetary algorithms serve different practical needs.

translations.literal: Jiang Ji used lunar eclipses to check the lodge where the sun stood, and calendarists took him as their model.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Ji’s eclipse triangulation of solar longitude became authoritative for later specialists.

sentences.zh: 又著《渾天論》，以步日于黃道，駁前儒之失，並得其中矣。

translations.literal: He also wrote the *Treatise on the Armillary Heaven*, pacing the sun along the yellow road and refuting earlier scholars’ errors, altogether hitting the mean.
translations.idiomatic: His *Huntian lun* corrected prior armillary theory by tracking the ecliptic accurately.
